text:
應天府鄉試錄序
應天府鄉試錄錄嘉靖丁酉秋
應天府所貢士若文以
獻者也先是府臣疏
請考試官
上以命左諭德臣汝璧洗馬臣衢臣旣
被
===
命兼程而南也胥飭以規曰休茲知
恤哉敢告執事比至則同考試
爲學正臣文奎臣舉教諭臣尚忠臣
烈臣士翹臣州臣隆盛臣禹卿訓導臣
忠孚皆應聘以待矣又胥飭以規
曰艱茲協恭哉敢告同事比入
院則規條整豫式廓奕新爲監

恤哉敢告執事比至則同考試
爲學正〔臣文奎臣舉〕教諭〔臣尚忠臣〕
〔烈臣士翹臣州臣隆盛臣禹卿〕訓導〔臣〕

punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序

應天府鄉試錄，錄嘉靖丁酉秋應天府所貢士若文以獻者也。先是，府臣疏請考試官，上以命左諭德臣汝璧、洗馬臣衢。臣旣被命，兼程而南也，胥飭以規曰：「休茲知恤哉！敢告執事。」比至，則同考試爲學正臣文奎、臣舉，教諭臣尚忠、臣烈、臣士翹、臣州、臣隆盛、臣禹卿，訓導臣忠孚，皆應聘以待矣。又胥飭以規曰：「艱茲協恭哉！敢告同事。」比入院，則規條整豫，式廓奕新，爲監
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

The Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination records the scholars recommended by Yingtian Prefecture, together with their essays, for presentation to the throne in the autumn of the dingyou year of Jiajing [1537]. Previously, the prefectural officials had submitted a memorial requesting Examiners. His Majesty thereupon appointed your servants Rubi, Left Admonisher, and Qu, Librarian in the Household of the Heir Apparent. Having received the command, we hastened south, traveling by forced stages. We admonished one another with these words: “This is an auspicious undertaking; recognize the need for solicitude[?]! We venture to address this admonition to those charged with the task.”

When we arrived, the Associate Examiners had all accepted their invitations and were awaiting us: your servants Wenkui and Ju, Instructors; Shangzhong, Lie, Shiqiao, Zhou, Longsheng, and Yuqing, Instructors; and Zhongfu, Assistant Instructor. Again we admonished one another: “This is a difficult undertaking; unite in reverent service! We venture to address this admonition to our colleagues.” When we entered the examination compound, its regulations were well ordered and prepared in advance, and its layout spacious and splendidly renewed[?], through the work of the supervising …

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
試御史臣宏臣應陽之所擘畫提
調府尹臣懋之所恢拓者業有
成勞矣而府丞臣祺寔繼之則
又胥飭以規曰允廸兹恤且恭
哉敢藉以告成事乃合六館諸
曹曁提學御史臣馮天馭之所簡
士凡四千五百有奇三試而三
===
校之遵
制額斂其才一百三十有五人其
限於額而不能畢斂者亦多矣
於戲盛哉臣惟才之需於世也
猶諸嘉穀美植然顧地有宜焉
以産也時有候焉以成也壤積
而膏流氣鬯而實遂其盛乃臻
alt_text:
試御史臣宏臣應陽之所擘畫提
調府尹臣懋之所恢拓者業有
成勞矣而府丞臣麒寔繼之則
又胥飭以規曰允迪茲恤且恭
哉敢藉以告成事乃合六館諸
曹暨提學御史臣馮天馭之所簡
士凡四千五百有奇三試而三
===
校之遵
制額歛其才一百三十有五人其
限於額而不能畢歛者亦多矣
於戲盛哉臣惟才之需於世也
猶諸嘉穀美植然顧地有宜焉
以產也時有候焉以成也壤積
而膏流氣鬯而實遂其盛乃臻
punctuated:
試御史臣宏、臣應陽之所擘畫，提調府尹臣懋之所恢拓者，業有成勞矣。而府丞臣祺寔繼之，則又胥飭以規曰：「允廸兹恤且恭哉！」敢藉以告成事。乃合六館諸曹曁提學御史臣馮天馭之所簡士，凡四千五百有奇，三試而三校之。遵制額，斂其才一百三十有五人，其限於額而不能畢斂者亦多矣。於戲，盛哉！
臣惟才之需於世也，猶諸嘉穀美植然。顧地有宜焉，以産也；時有候焉，以成也。壤積而膏流，氣鬯而實遂，其盛乃臻
translation_en:
…the arrangements devised by your servants Hong and Yingyang, the Censors supervising the examination, and the facilities expanded by your servant Mao, the Prefect serving as Proctor, had already been brought to completion through their labors. Your servant Qi, the Prefectural Vice Administrator, duly carried on their work. We then again admonished one another with this injunction: “Truly practice this solicitude and reverence!” We venture on this basis to report the completion of our task. We assembled the scholars selected by the various offices of the Six Colleges [?] and by your servant Feng Tianyu, the Censor supervising education, numbering more than 4,500 in all. We examined them in three sessions and assessed them three times. In accordance with the prescribed quota, we selected 135 talented men. There were also many whom the quota prevented us from including. Ah, how abundant was the talent!
Your servant considers that talent, which the world needs, resembles fine grain and flourishing plants. The soil must be suitable for them to grow, and the season must provide the right conditions for them to mature. When the soil accumulates and its fertility flows, when the vital energies circulate freely and the fruits develop fully, their abundance then reaches its height…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也二者間一弗值焉於是乎均
是需也而墳壚而華離則無必
產矣均是產也而游息而朘薄
則無必成矣幸而成焉遷乎其
性而索乎其爲利世之需之者
固亦微云爾已矣於戲才之盛
也其難矣乎臣觀於是而有以
===
知
今日之才之盛之繇矣盖南畿之
勝啓自六朝然卒偏安一隅而
光嶽之氣亦因之以分惟我
高皇帝龍飛淮甸肇迹是都遂用之
以混一海宇而東南諸郡皆進
爲畿輔其磅礴鬱積之氣盖蓄

也二者間一弗偵焉於是乎均
是需也而墳壚而華離則無必
產矣均是產也而游息而膄薄
則無必成矣幸而成焉遷乎其
性而索乎其爲利世之需之者
固亦徵云爾已矣於戲才之盛

===
知
今日之才之盛之繇矣蓋南畿之
勝啓自六朝然卒偏安一隅而
光嶽之氣亦因之以分惟我
高皇帝龍飛淮甸肇迹是都遂用之
以混一海宇而東南諸郡皆進
爲畿輔其磅礴鬱積之氣蓋蓄
punctuated:
也。二者間一弗值焉，於是乎均是需也，而墳壚而華離，則無必產矣；均是產也，而游息而朘薄，則無必成矣。幸而成焉，遷乎其性而索乎其爲利，世之需之者固亦微云爾已矣。於戲！才之盛也，其難矣乎！臣觀於是，而有以知今日之才之盛之繇矣。
盖南畿之勝啓自六朝，然卒偏安一隅，而光嶽之氣亦因之以分。惟我高皇帝龍飛淮甸，肇迹是都，遂用之以混一海宇，而東南諸郡皆進爲畿輔。其磅礴鬱積之氣，盖蓄
translation_en:
…Only then does abundance reach its fullness. If either of these two conditions is lacking, then, though the need is the same, differences in soil and separation [?] mean that production cannot be assured; though something is produced, neglect and depletion mean that its maturation cannot be assured. Even if it fortunately reaches maturity, if its nature is altered and profit is wrung from it, its usefulness to the world will surely be slight indeed. Alas! How difficult it is for talent to flourish! Reflecting on this, your servant has come to understand why talent flourishes so abundantly today.
The eminence of the southern metropolitan region began with the Six Dynasties. Yet they ultimately maintained their rule in only one corner of the realm, and the vital energies of the land were consequently divided as well. Our Emperor Gao rose like a dragon in the Huai region and established the foundations of his rule in this capital. Using it as his base, he unified all within the seas, and the prefectures of the southeast were all raised to the status of the metropolitan region. Its vast, concentrated vital energies had surely been accumulating…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之久矣我
文皇帝則又奠鼎於北南嚮而聽治
焉於是兩都對峙而豐芑之仁
視外服寔先首被則所以封殖
而濬發之者抑又獨至矣詩曰
思皇多士生此王國其地產有
固然與
===
列聖紹休益勤溉息至我
皇上涵濡振率風行海流盖又十有
六年于兹矣其間
明倫盡制
稽古右文卓乎中正以觀天下間
嘗
躬御

嘗
躬御

之久矣。我文皇帝則又奠鼎於北，南嚮而聽治焉。於是兩都對峙，而豐芑之仁，視外服寔先首被，則所以封殖而濬發之者，抑又獨至矣。《詩》曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。」其地產有固然與？
列聖紹休，益勤溉息。至我皇上，涵濡振率，風行海流，盖又十有六年于兹矣。其間明倫盡制，稽古右文，卓乎中正，以觀天下。間嘗躬御
translation_en:
…had accumulated for a long time. Our Emperor Wen then established his capital in the north, where he faced south and attended to government. Thus the two capitals stood facing one another; compared with the outlying territories, they were indeed the first to receive the benevolence that nurtures talent, like luxuriant millet. The means employed to cultivate and bring forth that accumulated vitality were therefore exceptionally thorough. The Book of Odes says: “How splendid the many worthy men, born in this royal realm!” Might there be something inherent in this land’s production of such men?
Successive sage emperors continued this glorious legacy, attending ever more diligently to its nourishment and growth [?]. Under our present emperor, nurturing influence and vigorous leadership have spread like the wind and flowed like the sea for sixteen years now. During this time, he has clarified human relationships and fully established institutions, studied antiquity and honored literary culture, standing preeminent in centrality and rectitude as an example for all under Heaven. On occasion, he has personally wielded…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
宸翰
詔迪膠庠則又粹乎精一執中之
微言是以神化之妙潜孚默奪
雖夫人而皆興至於士則可知
矣至於首善之地之士則又可
知矣易曰聖人久於其道而天
下化成兹又其時也非與用是
===
敦厖純固之氣不鍾于物而鍾
于才盖有弘者毅者馮者翼者
雝以肅者奇以正者襃而實者
淵邃而敷達者而崇經黜子尊
王賤伯上義下利之趨靡不於
文乎見之即其委和之液滲而
爲嘉穀爲美植流衍四出亦足

矣至於首善之地之士則又可
知矣易曰聖人久於其道而天
下化成玆又其時也非與用是
===
敦厖純固之氣不鍾于物而鍾
于才盖有弘者毅者馮者翼者
雖以肅者奇以正者裦而實者
淵邃而敷達者而崇經黜子尊
王賤伯上義下利之趨靡不於
文乎見之即其委和之液滲而
爲嘉穀爲美植流衍四出亦足
punctuated: 宸翰，詔迪膠庠，則又粹乎精一執中之微言。是以神化之妙，潜孚默奪，雖夫人而皆興，至於士則可知矣；至於首善之地之士，則又可知矣。《易》曰：「聖人久於其道，而天下化成。」兹又其時也，非與？用是敦厖純固之氣，不鍾于物而鍾于才。盖有弘者、毅者、馮者、翼者、雝以肅者、奇以正者、襃而實者、淵邃而敷達者，而崇經黜子、尊王賤伯、上義下利之趨，靡不於文乎見之。即其委和之液，滲而爲嘉穀、爲美植，流衍四出，亦足
translation_en: …with his imperial brush, he issued edicts to instruct the schools, distilling the subtle teachings of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the mean. Thus the wondrous efficacy of his transforming influence has quietly won trust and imperceptibly changed hearts. Even ordinary people have all been stirred to better themselves; how much more, then, the scholars! And how much more the scholars of this place foremost in moral example! The Book of Changes says: “The sage abides long in his Way, and all under Heaven are transformed and brought to completion.” Is this not another such time? Consequently, this generous, abundant, pure, and steadfast vital force gathers not in things but in talented men. Among them are those who are broad-minded, resolute, forceful [?], circumspect, harmonious yet solemn, original yet correct, expansive yet substantial, and profound yet lucid in expression. Their inclination to exalt the Classics and subordinate the writings of the masters, to honor true kingship and deprecate hegemony, and to place righteousness above profit is invariably evident in their writing. Indeed, the fluid essence of this accumulated harmony seeps forth to produce fine grain and flourishing plants; spreading outward in every direction, it too suffices to…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
以衣被乎天下則
今日之才之盛也豈偶然而致哉
雖然産才者地也惟才也斯成
地之能成才者時也惟才也斯
翊時之運交相賛者也故臣於
是舉以告成事既以得才爲
朝廷賀以端始進則以究才爲諸
===
士期俾其知所生之地所際之
時如是之不偶也庶幾出而効
用也必樹勲流聲俾地望爲之
益重必奮庸熈載俾時運爲之
益隆庶於
皇上求才之意爲不負而東南得才
之盛將益光昭于無窮臣等區

朝廷賀以端始進則以究才爲諸

士期俾其知所生之地所際之
時如是之不偶也庶幾出而效
用也必樹勳流聲俾地望爲之
益重必奮庸熈載俾時運爲之
益隆庶於
皇上求才之意爲不負而東南得才
之盛將益光昭于無窮臣等區
punctuated: 以衣被乎天下，則今日之才之盛也，豈偶然而致哉？雖然，産才者地也，惟才也斯成地之能；成才者時也，惟才也斯翊時之運，交相賛者也。故臣於是舉以告成事，既以得才爲朝廷賀，以端始進，則以究才爲諸士期，俾其知所生之地、所際之時，如是之不偶也。庶幾出而効用也，必樹勲流聲，俾地望爲之益重；必奮庸熈載，俾時運爲之益隆。庶於皇上求才之意爲不負，而東南得才之盛，將益光昭于無窮。臣等區
translation_en: …to clothe and shelter all under Heaven. Could the present abundance of talent, then, have come about by chance? Yet it is the land that produces talent, and only through talent is the land’s capacity fulfilled; it is the age that brings talent to maturity, and only through talent is the course of the age advanced. They assist one another. Thus, in reporting the completion of this examination, I congratulate the court on having obtained talented men; and, to set their first steps into official life on the proper course, I charge these gentlemen with fully realizing their talents. Let them understand how far from accidental are the land of their birth and the age they have encountered. When they come forth to serve, may they establish achievements and leave an enduring reputation, thereby adding to the prestige of their native land; may they exert themselves in service and bring their undertakings to fruition, thereby further advancing the fortunes of the age. In this way, they may live up to His Majesty’s intention in seeking talent, and the southeast’s abundant harvest of talented men will shine ever more brightly for all time. We, your servants, …

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
區掄才之忠庶亦賴是以少効
也已嗚呼諸士其懋諸其亦胥
飭以規諸
奉直大夫左春坊左諭德江汝璧
謹序
alt_text:
區掄才之忠庶亦頼是以少効
也巳嗚呼諸士其懋諸其亦胥
飭以規諸
奉直大夫左春坊左諭德江〔汝璧〕
謹序
punctuated:
區掄才之忠，庶亦賴是以少効也已。嗚呼！諸士其懋諸，其亦胥飭以規諸！
奉直大夫、左春坊左諭德江汝璧謹序。
translation_en:
…our humble devotion to selecting talent may thereby also achieve some small result. Ah! You scholars, strive diligently, and admonish one another so as to keep one another on the proper course!
Preface respectfully composed by Jiang Rubi, Grand Master for Upright Service and Left Mentor of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.

translation_en:
Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination, the sixteenth year of Jiajing (1537)

Proctors

Sun Mao, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture. His courtesy name was Defu; he was from Cixi County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the xinwei year.

Yang Qi, Vice Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture. His courtesy name was Renfu; he was from Shangrao County, Jiangxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.

Examiners

Jiang Rubi, Grand Master for Forthright Service and Left Exhorter in the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent. His courtesy name was Maogu; he was from Guixi County, Jiangxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.

Ouyang Qu, Grand Master for Forthright Service and Librarian in the Classics and Documents Office. His courtesy name was Chongheng; he was from Taihe County, Jiangxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Associate Examiners

Shu Wenkui, School Instructor at the Confucian school of Yuanzhou Subprefecture, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Daoguang; he was from Quanzhou Subprefecture, Guangxi, and was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the yiyou year.

Qian Ju, School Instructor at the Confucian school of Shanzhou Subprefecture, Henan Prefecture, Henan. His courtesy name was Xuancai; he was from Jiangjin County, Sichuan, and was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.

Tang Shangzhong, School Instructor at the Confucian school of Liaocheng County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. His courtesy name was Yaochen; he was from Shunde County, Guangdong, and was a tribute scholar of the wuzi year.

Ouyang Lie, School Instructor at the Confucian school of Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. His courtesy name was Maozhi; he was from Taihe County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute scholar of the renwu year.

Liang Shiqiao, School Instructor at the Confucian school of Ouning County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. His courtesy name was Yuanbiao; he was from Nanhai County, Guangdong, and was a tribute scholar of the yiyou year.

Xu Zhou, School Instructor at the Confucian school of Yiyang County, Ruzhou Subprefecture, Henan. His courtesy name was Bangcai; he was registered with the Yunnan Front Guard, was originally from Renhe County, Zhejiang, and was a tribute scholar of the jiawu year.

Zhou Longsheng, School Instructor at the Confucian school of Yingshan County, Suizhou Subprefecture, De'an Prefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Daoheng; he was from Pingle County, Guangxi, and was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.

Zhang Yuqing, School Instructor at the Confucian school of Youxi County, Yanping Prefecture, Fujian. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he held officer-household registration in the Guangxi Escort Guard, was originally from Wuling County, Huguang, and was a tribute scholar of the wuzi year.

Yang Zhongfu, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian school of Zhaoqing Prefecture, Guangdong. His courtesy name was Zhuxin; he was from Putian County, Fujian, and was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.

Examination Inspectors

Officials in charge of collecting and keeping examination scripts:
Wang Qing, Grand Master for Governance and Administrative Assistant of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yongqing. He was from Dingzhou Guard in Zhili and was a tribute scholar of the bingzi year.
Yang Ziqin, Gentleman for Conferring Virtue and Assistant Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Kexiu. He was from Xinzheng County, Henan, and was a tribute scholar of the guiyou year.

Officials in charge of stamping examination scripts:
Gan Chun, Gentleman for Conferring Virtue and Assistant Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ziye. He was from Luoyang County, Henan, and was a tribute scholar of the guiyou year.
Hu Zhou, Gentleman for Undertaking Service and Judge of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Dengzhi. He was registered in an officer household of Yingchuan Guard, Henan, and was a tribute scholar of the gengwu year.

Officials in charge of receiving examination scripts:
Zhou Wei, Magistrate of Liuhe County in Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Weihan. He was from Yin County, Zhejiang, and was a tribute scholar of the jimao year [?; transcribed 已卯].

Officials in charge of sealing identifying information:

Chen Guanghua, Magistrate of Lishui County in Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Daoyun. He was from Putian County, Fujian, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year [?; transcribed 已丑].

text:
第壹場
四書
詩云樂只君子民之父母民之所好好之
民之所惡惡之此之謂民之父母
子曰回也其心三月不違仁其餘則日月至焉而已矣
必有事焉而勿正心勿忘勿助長也
易
无妄剛自外來而為主於內動而健剛中
===
而應大亨以正天之命也
六五貞吉无悔君子之光有孚吉
是以明於天之道而察於民之故是興神
物以前民用聖人以此齊戒以神明其
德夫
聖人之大寶曰位
書
帝庸作歌曰勅天之命惟時惟幾乃歌曰
股肱喜哉元首起哉百工熙哉臯陶拜

punctuated:
第壹場

四書

《詩》云：「樂只君子，民之父母。」民之所好好之，民之所惡惡之，此之謂民之父母。

子曰：「回也，其心三月不違仁，其餘則日月至焉而已矣。」

必有事焉而勿正，心勿忘，勿助長也。

易

无妄，剛自外來而為主於內，動而健，剛中而應，大亨以正，天之命也。

六五，貞吉，无悔。君子之光，有孚，吉。

是以明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物以前民用。聖人以此齊戒，以神明其德夫！

聖人之大寶曰位。

書

帝庸作歌曰：「勅天之命，惟時惟幾。」乃歌曰：「股肱喜哉！元首起哉！百工熙哉！」臯陶拜
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Book of Odes says: “Joyful is the noble man, the father and mother of the people.” To love what the people love and hate what the people hate: this is what it means to be the father and mother of the people.

The Master said: “As for Hui, his heart did not depart from benevolence for three months. The others attain it only for a day or a month at a time.”

One must keep working at it without anticipating the result; the heart must neither forget it nor help it grow by force.

Book of Changes

Without Falsehood: the firm comes from outside and becomes master within. There is movement and strength; the firm occupies the central position and finds a response. Great success through correctness is Heaven’s mandate.

Six in the fifth place: perseverance brings good fortune; there is no regret. The noble man’s radiance: sincerity brings good fortune.

Thus, understanding the Way of Heaven and discerning the circumstances of the people, they brought forth sacred objects to lead the people in their use. Through these the sages purified themselves and observed abstinence, thereby making their virtue spiritually luminous!

The sage’s greatest treasure is called his position.

Book of Documents

The emperor thereupon composed a song, saying: “Attend reverently to Heaven’s mandate; be mindful of the times and of the first stirrings of events.” Then he sang: “When the limbs rejoice, the head rises, and the hundred officials flourish!” Gao Yao bowed …

translation_en:
…with hands joined, bowed his head to the ground and declared: “Be mindful! In leading undertakings and initiating affairs, be careful of your rules. Be reverent! Repeatedly examine your accomplishments. Be reverent!” Then he continued the song: “When the head is enlightened, the limbs are worthy, and all affairs prosper!”
Regulate affairs by righteousness; regulate the heart by ritual propriety.
Furthermore, Kings Wen and Wu could discern the hearts of those occupying the three classes of office and clearly perceive the hearts of the outstanding men in those three classes. Thus they reverently served the Lord on High and established leaders and chiefs for the people.
I therefore bestow upon you one you-vessel of black-millet sacrificial wine, one red bow, one hundred red arrows, one black bow, and one hundred black arrows.
The Book of Odes
Joyful is the gentleman; blessings bring him fulfillment.
The spirits have come and bestowed many blessings upon you. The people are settled, daily eating and drinking. All the common people everywhere follow your virtue.
Strength lies in worthy men; the four quarters take instruction from them. When virtue and conduct are upright and great, the states of the four quarters follow them. Grand plans establish the decrees; far-reaching counsels are announced at the proper time. Reverent and careful in your dignified bearing, you are the model for the people.
From the hall to its foundation, from sheep to oxen, there are great cauldrons, ordinary cauldrons, and small cauldrons.
The Spring and Autumn Annals
In summer, Zhongqiu was fortified. 〔Seventh year of Duke Yin.〕 In winter, Mei was built. 〔Duke Zhuang’s twenty-…〕

…What is manifest yet unmoving is earth; what alternates between movement and stillness lies between heaven and earth. Thus the sage speaks of ritual and music.
To offer a sacrificial feast is to turn toward its recipient in reverence; only after doing so can one offer the feast.
The Son of Heaven forms a triad with heaven and earth. Thus his virtue matches heaven and earth, bringing benefit to all things alike. He shines together with the sun and moon, his light illuminating all within the four seas and overlooking nothing, however small.

問：自古帝王建極垂統，類有謨訓以衍無疆之休。若唐虞之禪位命官，三代之傳緒敷訓，固已列諸典謨訓誥，炳然垂之萬世而爲經。嗣是以還，雖有《法術》《帝範》《要畧》之詒，《理人》《訓廉》《謹刑》之式，然其爲訓則寢以微矣。洪惟我宣宗章皇帝，典學之餘，有得于我祖宗《資世通訓》《聖學心法》之書之旨，作爲《帝訓》《官箴》，以對揚二聖之光訓，誠萬世聖子神孫及我臣工所當佩習而服行之者也。
translation_en:
Submitting statements on the virtuous governance of high officials.
Inspecting disaster-damaged fields and their grain-tax assessments.
Diviners making unfounded predictions of misfortune and good fortune.
Controlling the entry and exit of palace eunuchs.
Failing to repair dikes at the proper time.

Third Session
Policy questions 〔five questions〕

Question: Since antiquity, emperors and kings, in establishing the supreme standard and transmitting their succession, have generally provided counsels and instructions to perpetuate blessings without limit. Such matters as the abdications and appointments to office under Tang and Yu, and the transmission of succession and promulgation of instruction under the Three Dynasties, were already set forth in the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements, shining forth for all generations as scripture. Thereafter, although there were the bequeathed teachings of Laws and Methods (Fashu) [?], Models for Emperors (Difan), and Essential Outlines (Yaolüe), and the precedents of Governing the People (Liren), Instructions on Integrity (Xunlian), and Caution in Punishment (Jinxing), their force as instruction gradually diminished.

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Xuanzong, posthumously honored as Zhang, in the time remaining from his classical studies, grasped the purport of our ancestral emperors’ books, Comprehensive Instructions for Aiding the World (Zishi tongxun) and Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa). He composed Instructions for Emperors (Dixun) and Admonitions for Officials (Guanzhen), thereby answering and extolling the illustrious teachings of the two sages. These are indeed works that sagely sons and divine descendants through all generations, together with us officials, ought to cherish, study, and put into practice.

translation_en:
…Yet may you extol and expound the subtle expressions and profound meanings within them that complement the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements of antiquity? The arrangement by category and tables of contents of these two books, together with the profound imperial intentions behind their composition, have already been set forth in imperially written prefaces at their beginning. May you also elucidate these? The Instructions are preserved in the imperial archives and are indeed not easily accessible for reverent examination. Yet the Confucian officials of that time did compile them into a Collection of Imperial Writings. As for the Admonitions, they are engraved in the various government offices: who has not studied and become familiar with them? Moreover, you scholars will soon bear responsibility for guiding your ruler toward perfection and serving in office. Please respectfully expound these matters in your response.

Question: Master Liu said, “The great affairs of a state lie in sacrifice and warfare.” Those who aspire to administer a state must understand them. Confucius also said, “When I fight, I prevail; when I sacrifice, I receive blessings.” Thus, those who have not grasped the proper Way of these matters cannot participate in understanding them either. May we now bring forward their principal and most essential aspects and discuss and ascertain them together [?]? Speaking of sacrificial affairs, His Majesty recently rectified the rites of the suburban sacrifices and the ancestral temples. This truly accords with the saying, “Established before Heaven and Earth without contradiction, examined before the ghosts and spirits and…”

大禘
大祫之祭
皇上亦既親定而舉千有餘年之廢典矣顧祔食
從享之節亦無有待於裁定者乎以戎
事言之頃者
皇上撤毀佛寺議欲改制以閱武事是將布昭
聖武以覲耿光以揚大烈矣然觀諸今武學有
肄會選有條武舉有科
punctuated:
無疑者矣。然稽諸古，周人郊祀后稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂以配上帝。不知我祖宗分配之儀，亦可準是而行之否乎？間嘗伏讀聖諭，謂於歲首仍祀上帝於大祀殿，以文皇帝奉配，乃今稍異焉，豈以祀殿、明堂制不可以相準已乎？至於大禘、大祫之祭，皇上亦既親定，而舉千有餘年之廢矣。顧祔食、從享之節，亦無有待於裁定者乎？

以戎事言之，頃者皇上撤毁佛寺，議欲改制以閱武事，是將布昭聖武，以覲耿光，以揚大烈矣。然觀諸今，武學有肄，會選有條，武舉有科，
translation_en:
…and leave no room for doubt. Yet, examining antiquity, the people of Zhou offered suburban sacrifices to Hou Ji as the associate of Heaven, and honored King Wen with ancestral sacrifices in the Hall of Light (Mingtang) as the associate of the Supreme Deity. Might our own rites assigning ancestral emperors as associates likewise be conducted according to this precedent? Some time ago, I reverently read the imperial instruction stating that, at the beginning of the year, sacrifices would continue to be offered to the Supreme Deity in the Hall of the Great Sacrifice, with Emperor Wen as his associate. Now, however, the arrangement differs somewhat. Is this because the institutions of the sacrificial hall and the Hall of Light cannot be treated as equivalent? As for the great di and great xia ancestral sacrifices, His Majesty has already personally determined their rites and revived observances that had fallen into disuse for more than a thousand years. Yet are there no details concerning those admitted to share the offerings and those receiving subsidiary offerings that still await authoritative determination?

Turning to military affairs, His Majesty recently had a Buddhist temple demolished and discussed altering its arrangement for reviewing military exercises. This will manifest his sagely martial prowess, display his brilliant glory, and proclaim his great achievements. Yet, considering present arrangements, the military schools provide training, the assembled selection of military personnel has its regulations, and the military examinations have their established categories…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之令甲具設矣及至分閫置帥輒厪
當宁乏材之歎果何繇歟
祖宗時弛備有罰亡伍有謫團練有法今品式
固在也而頃遇有警又勤募兵之
令豈所養者舉不足用歟茲於二者欲一飭
而振之又何道歟夫秩祀修戎經文緯
武之理也非豪傑士可易易而談哉惟
無效書生之常談斯可矣
問漢儒有云人君所爲美惡之極與天地
===
相爲流通而往來相應其見卓矣今姑
就漢論之孝文之時災異疊見乃無損
於其治孝武之時祥瑞日至竟不能救
海內之虛耗豈天道深遠難見而感應
有不足信歟宋儒有三不盡之說謂爲
享國長久之道深取於文而不足於武
似有所見抑於災祥之理有相關歟我
太祖高皇帝創業艱難克謹天戒凡遇災祥一
切警懼不知於斯三者嘗加之意否歟

海内之虛耗豈天道深遠難見而感應
有不足信歟宋儒有三不盡之說謂爲
享國長久之道深取於文而不足於武
似有所見抑於災祥之理有相關歟我
太祖高皇帝創業艱難克謹天戒凡遇災祥一
切警懼不知於斯三者嘗加之意否歟
punctuated:
祖宗之令甲具設矣，及至分閫置帥，輒厪當宁乏材之歎，果何繇歟？祖宗時，弛備有罰，亡伍有謫，團練有法。今品式固在也，而頃遇有警，又勤募兵之令，豈所養者舉不足用歟？茲於二者，欲一飭而振之，又何道歟？夫秩祀修戎，經文緯武之理也，非豪傑士可易易而談哉？惟無效書生之常談，斯可矣。
問：漢儒有云：「人君所爲美惡之極，與天地相爲流通，而往來相應。」其見卓矣！今姑就漢論之，孝文之時，災異疊見，乃無損於其治；孝武之時，祥瑞日至，竟不能救海內之虛耗。豈天道深遠難見，而感應有不足信歟？宋儒有三不盡之說，謂爲享國長久之道，深取於文而不足於武，似有所見，抑於災祥之理有相關歟？我太祖高皇帝創業艱難，克謹天戒，凡遇災祥，一切警懼，不知於斯三者嘗加之意否歟？
translation_en:
…The statutes of the imperial ancestors are all in place. Yet whenever regional military commands are assigned and commanders appointed, His Majesty is invariably troubled enough to lament the lack of capable men. What, indeed, is the reason? Under the imperial ancestors, there were penalties for neglecting military preparedness, punishments for deserting the ranks, and regulations for organizing and training troops. These established rules certainly remain in force today. Yet when an alarm recently arose, His Majesty again had to issue an order to recruit soldiers. Could it be that all the troops maintained by the state are unfit for service? By what means might these two matters—sacrificial observances and military preparedness—be set in order and reinvigorated together? Ordering sacrifices and attending to military affairs embody the principle of weaving civil and military government together as warp and weft. Can anyone who is not a man of outstanding ability discuss them readily? Simply refrain from repeating the commonplace talk of bookish scholars, and that will suffice.
Question: A Han Confucian scholar said: “The utmost good and evil in a ruler’s actions circulate between him and Heaven and Earth, responding to one another in their passage back and forth.” His insight was outstanding! For now, let us consider the Han alone. During Emperor Xiaowen’s reign, disasters and anomalies appeared repeatedly, yet did no harm to his good government. During Emperor Xiaowu’s reign, auspicious signs arrived daily, yet ultimately could not avert the depletion of the realm. Could it be that the Way of Heaven is profound, remote, and difficult to discern, and that the correspondence between human actions and heavenly responses is not entirely trustworthy? A Song Confucian scholar advanced the doctrine of the “three things not to exhaust,” calling it the way to ensure a dynasty’s long endurance. He greatly approved of Emperor Wen in this regard but found Emperor Wu wanting. This seems to reflect some insight; might it also bear upon the principles governing disasters and auspicious signs? Our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty amid hardship and was scrupulously attentive to Heaven’s warnings. Whenever disasters or auspicious signs appeared, he invariably remained vigilant and apprehensive. We wonder whether he ever gave particular attention to these three things.

punctuated:
方今聖明在上，懋德建中，修政導和，諸福之物莫不畢至，已禁天下勿復以聞。頃因後殿之災，罷安南之征，停沙河之工，詔三大臣審錄繫囚，誠不忍盡是三者之仁心也。固不啻弭災致祥而已，宗社億萬年無疆之休，端有賴焉。吾曹百執事祗承德意，思以補裨於萬一，不知交修之道，其實果安在歟？爾多士明於當時之務，幸有以告我。

問：有國則有用，雖堯舜不能不取諸民。《禹貢》之差田賦，《周禮》遂人、匠人之所掌，其法尚矣。秦廢井田，取民無制。漢承其後，悉除秦法，而井田獨未之復，何歟？漢初十五稅一，其後三十稅一，又其後筭舟
translation_en:
At present, our sage and enlightened sovereign reigns above, assiduously cultivating virtue and establishing the mean, improving government and fostering harmony. Every kind of auspicious object has appeared in abundance, and he has already forbidden all under Heaven to report any more of them to him. Recently, because of the disaster at the rear palace hall, he called off the campaign against Annan, halted the construction works at Shahe, and ordered three high ministers to review the cases of imprisoned persons. This truly expresses his benevolent heart, which cannot bear to exhaust these three things. It does more than merely avert calamities and bring auspicious signs: upon it indeed depends the boundless prosperity of the ancestral temples and the altars of state for countless ages. We officials reverently receive his virtuous intentions and hope to contribute even the smallest assistance. Yet wherein, in practice, does the way of mutual correction and improvement truly lie? You assembled scholars understand the affairs of the present time; please instruct us.

Question: A state necessarily has expenditures; even Yao and Shun could not avoid collecting resources from the people. The grading of land and its taxes in the Tribute of Yu, and the responsibilities of the Directors of the Outer Suburbs (suiren) and Master Craftsmen (jiangren) in the Rites of Zhou, represent institutions of great antiquity. Qin abolished the well-field system and imposed no limits on what it exacted from the people. Han succeeded it and abolished all Qin laws, yet alone failed to restore the well-field system. Why was this? Early in the Han, one part in fifteen was levied; later, one part in thirty. Still later, taxes were assessed on boats…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
車榷鹽鐵竟不聞有加賦之議何歟唐
初以租庸調取民其後也變爲兩稅陸
贄諸人極言其非而亦有謂未可盡非
之者何歟宋初取民多因唐制其後也
變更修復亦有彼善於此者可得而悉
言歟我
朝田賦之制監於三代而損益之百七十年
國富民裕然江南之地取給什九昔人謂之
陸海信矣邇來逋負日甚征斂日急加
===
之水旱凶荒民不聊生議者或曰不減
田額不均田則不可以善其後或曰國
用有經民習有常其孰執紛更怨訕之
咎或曰
先朝嘗減額矣今亦須視其時或曰治道去
其太甚均則今當有漸是四說者將安
取衷哉諸士子生長於斯其於利病因
革之宜必有至當畫一之論幸詳言之
以觀先憂之志

punctuated: 車、榷鹽鐵，竟不聞有加賦之議，何歟？唐初以租庸調取民，其後也變爲兩稅，陸贄諸人極言其非，而亦有謂未可盡非之者，何歟？宋初取民多因唐制，其後也變更修復，亦有彼善於此者，可得而悉言歟？我朝田賦之制，監於三代而損益之，百七十年，國富民裕。然江南之地，取給什九，昔人謂之陸海，信矣！邇來逋負日甚，征斂日急，加之水旱凶荒，民不聊生。議者或曰：「不減田額，不均田則，不可以善其後。」或曰：「國用有經，民習有常，其孰執紛更怨訕之咎？」或曰：「先朝嘗減額矣，今亦須視其時。」或曰：「治道去其太甚，均則今當有漸。」是四說者，將安取衷哉？諸士子生長於斯，其於利病因革之宜，必有至當畫一之論，幸詳言之，以觀先憂之志。
translation_en:
…carts, and imposed monopolies on salt and iron, yet we hear of no proposal to increase the land tax. Why was this? At the beginning of the Tang, levies were collected from the people through the system of grain tax, labor service or its commutation, and payments in textiles. Later this was changed to the twice-yearly tax. Lu Zhi and others vehemently condemned it, yet some also maintained that it could not be condemned entirely. Why was this? At the beginning of the Song, levies on the people largely followed Tang institutions. Subsequent changes and restorations also included some measures better than others. Can you discuss them all in detail?

Our dynasty’s system of land taxation took the Three Dynasties as its model, making additions and reductions. For 170 years, the state has been wealthy and the people prosperous. Yet Jiangnan supplies nine-tenths of what is required. Earlier writers called it a “sea on land”—truly an apt description! Recently, tax arrears have grown ever greater and collection has become ever more pressing. Added to this are floods, droughts, crop failures, and famine: the people can no longer sustain their livelihoods.

Some who discuss the matter say: “Unless land-tax quotas are reduced and land-tax rates equalized, there can be no satisfactory resolution.” Others say: “State expenditure has established rules, and the people have settled habits. Who would bear the blame for disruptive changes and the resentment and criticism they provoke?” Others say: “Previous reigns have reduced the quotas. Now, too, we must consider the circumstances of the time.” Still others say: “The way to govern is to eliminate the worst excesses. Equalizing the rates should now proceed gradually.” How should a balanced judgment be reached among these four views? You examination candidates were born and raised here. Concerning benefits and harms, and what should properly be retained or changed, you must have thoroughly sound and coherent arguments. Please set them out in detail, so that we may see your resolve to take thought for the people’s troubles before others do.

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
問昔人有云禦戎無上策當以氣勝之若
今北圉告警南交不庭不可不思所以
禦之者將務以氣勝歟試借往事與諸
君一籌之彼漢高帝之困白登也時則
威加海內矣氣顧弗勝歟三傳而至武
帝威行匈奴氣則勝矣乃不免于輪臺
之悔何歟若閉關謝虜之光武則論者
方有取焉豈氣固不足事歟宋藝祖之
志復幽燕盖思一作其氣矣繼之者如
眞宗仁宗志不足以帥氣論者是以有
武事不競之譏則氣也誠不可不有所
事歟然神宗思一作之而卒蒙釀亂之
名抑又何歟豈所謂氣勝云者治之固
别有道歟仰惟
聖祖高皇帝汛掃胡元廓清函夏中原氣盛之
說嘗自揭於北征之檄矣是固天之所
畀而我
聖祖之所以持志治氣之道尤無不至也令亦

聖祖之所以持志治氣之道尤無不至也今亦
punctuated: 問：昔人有云：「禦戎無上策，當以氣勝之。」若今北圉告警，南交不庭，不可不思所以禦之者，將務以氣勝歟？試借往事，與諸君一籌之。彼漢高帝之困白登也，時則威加海內矣，氣顧弗勝歟？三傳而至武帝，威行匈奴，氣則勝矣，乃不免于輪臺之悔，何歟？若閉關謝虜之光武，則論者方有取焉，豈氣固不足事歟？宋藝祖之志復幽燕，盖思一作其氣矣。繼之者如眞宗、仁宗，志不足以帥氣，論者是以有武事不競之譏，則氣也誠不可不有所事歟？然神宗思一作之，而卒蒙釀亂之名，抑又何歟？豈所謂氣勝云者，治之固别有道歟？仰惟聖祖高皇帝汛掃胡元，廓清函夏，中原氣盛之說，嘗自揭於北征之檄矣。是固天之所畀，而我聖祖之所以持志治氣之道，尤無不至也。令亦
translation_en:
Question: A man of old once said, “There is no supreme strategy for resisting the Rong; one should overcome them through spirit.” Now that alarms come from the northern frontier and Jiaozhi in the south refuses submission, we cannot fail to consider how to resist them. Should we concentrate on prevailing through spirit? Let us draw on past events and deliberate together.

When Emperor Gao of Han was trapped at Baideng, his might already extended throughout the realm. Did his spirit nevertheless fail to prevail? After three imperial successions came Emperor Wu, whose might reached the Xiongnu: his spirit did prevail. Yet he could not escape the regrets expressed at Luntai. Why was this? As for Guangwu, who closed the frontier passes and rebuffed the northern peoples, commentators find merit in his conduct. Could it be that spirit is, after all, unworthy of cultivation?

The founding emperor of Song aspired to recover You and Yan, evidently intending to rouse that spirit. His successors, such as Zhenzong and Renzong, lacked the resolve to command their spirit, and commentators accordingly criticized their failure to excel in military affairs. Does this mean that spirit truly must be cultivated? Yet Shenzong sought to rouse it and ultimately acquired a reputation for fomenting disorder. Why, in turn, was this? Could it be that what is called “prevailing through spirit” requires a distinct way of governing that spirit?

Reverently considering our Sagely Progenitor, the Exalted Emperor: he swept away the alien Yuan and cleared the Chinese realm. In his proclamation for the northern expedition, he himself advanced the claim that the spirit of the Central Plain was flourishing. This was assuredly Heaven’s gift; yet our Sagely Progenitor’s methods for sustaining his resolve and governing his spirit were especially thorough in every respect. Now also [?]…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
可以頌言其萬一歟至于
祖訓一書又爲千萬世
聖子神孫而作者有曰胡元必謹備之則今三
邊六鎭之險亦有當修復之者歟將務
蓄材養氣以需之歟有曰安南不征則
宣廟誠得不治之治矣或謂
文廟固嘗治之又將安所適從歟其亦善持吾
志無動於氣歟且今南北之勢緩急堅
瑕有當權焉者執事者所願有聞也幸
===
極言之將以轉聞于
上

punctuated: 可以頌言其萬一歟？至于《祖訓》一書，又爲千萬世聖子神孫而作者，有曰：「胡元必謹備之。」則今三邊六鎭之險，亦有當修復之者歟？將務蓄材養氣以需之歟？有曰：「安南不征。」則宣廟誠得不治之治矣。或謂文廟固嘗治之，又將安所適從歟？其亦善持吾志，無動於氣歟？且今南北之勢，緩急堅瑕，有當權焉者，執事者所願有聞也。幸極言之，將以轉聞于上。
translation_en: …might one extol even a ten-thousandth part of it? As for the book Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun), written for his sagely sons and divine descendants throughout countless generations, it says: “Against the Mongol Yuan, one must maintain vigilant defenses.” Are there, then, strategic defenses in the Three Frontiers and Six Garrisons today that ought to be restored? Or should we concentrate on cultivating talent and nurturing martial spirit in readiness? It also says: “Annan is not to be attacked.” Thus Emperor Xuan indeed achieved order through nonintervention. Yet some say that Emperor Wen had certainly brought it under his rule. Which course, then, should we follow? Should we likewise maintain firm control of our resolve and not be swayed by our vital energies (qi)? Moreover, in the present strategic circumstances of north and south, there are matters of urgency and relative ease, strength and vulnerability, that require weighing. We who administer this examination wish to hear your views. Please expound them fully, so that we may convey them to His Majesty.

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
詩云樂只君子民之父母民之所好好之
民之所惡惡之此之謂民之父母
汪鴻儒
同考試官教諭歐陽批是善言父母斯民
之心者
同考試官教諭徐批辭不𧸛而意自足
可以式矣
===
考試官洗馬歐陽批純正
考試官左諭德江批典雅
傳者釋言君子之能子乎民以見其能絜矩也
蓋子民之道同其好惡而已矣自非絜矩之君
子其能然哉傳者釋詩之意蓋如此今夫尊莫
如君親莫如父母詩云樂只君子民之父母者
何哉誠以民生有欲孰無所好民好之而君不
之好則民亦安得而遂其所好乎亦孰無所惡
民惡之而君不之惡則民亦安得而違其所惡

punctuated:
第壹場

四書

詩云：「樂只君子，民之父母。」民之所好好之，民之所惡惡之，此之謂民之父母。

汪鴻儒

同考試官教諭歐陽批：「是善言父母斯民之心者。」

同考試官教諭徐批：「辭不𧸛而意自足，可以式矣。」

考試官洗馬歐陽批：「純正。」

考試官左諭德江批：「典雅。」

傳者釋言君子之能子乎民，以見其能絜矩也。蓋子民之道，同其好惡而已矣。自非絜矩之君子，其能然哉？傳者釋詩之意，蓋如此。今夫尊莫如君，親莫如父母。詩云：「樂只君子，民之父母」者，何哉？誠以民生有欲，孰無所好？民好之而君不之好，則民亦安得而遂其所好乎？亦孰無所惡？民惡之而君不之惡，則民亦安得而違其所惡
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Book of Odes says: “Joyful is the gentleman, the father and mother of the people.” To love what the people love and hate what the people hate: this is what it means to be the father and mother of the people.

Wang Hongru

Comment by Associate Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: “This expresses well the heart of one who acts as father and mother to these people.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “The wording is not excessive [?], yet the meaning is fully conveyed. It may serve as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Librarian to the Heir Apparent: “Pure and correct.”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Left Admonisher: “Classical and elegant.”

The commentator explains how the gentleman can treat the people as his children, thereby showing his ability to apply the measuring square—the principle of reciprocity. For the way to treat the people as one's children consists simply in sharing their likes and dislikes. Could anyone but a gentleman who applies the measuring square accomplish this? Such, in essence, is the commentator's explanation of the ode.

Now none is more exalted than the ruler, and none closer than one's father and mother. What does the ode mean when it says, “Joyful is the gentleman, the father and mother of the people”? Truly, people are born with desires: who has nothing they love? If the people love something but their ruler does not love it, how can they attain what they love? And who has nothing they hate? If the people hate something but their ruler does not hate it, how can they escape what they hate…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
乎爲民父母者必不若此也絜矩君子知民之
所好在是也則欲與之聚利與之開眞若有益
於我者而求必得之焉知民之所惡在是也則
事爲之制曲爲之防眞若有損于我者而求必
去之焉導之於生殖之間而施無不宜公之於
舉錯之際而處無不當若是者不謂之民之父
母而何哉誠以父母於子愛心眞切志固未始
有弗同天性至親情亦未始有弗合君子有以
通天下之志而好其所好則民之遂其好者亦
===
不忍以其所弗好者及之矣是雖分相遠也而
相親何以異於一體者乎有以順天下之情而
惡其所惡則民之違其惡者亦不忍以其所可
惡者及之矣是雖分相懸也而相愛有不同於
相生者乎所謂民之父母信然矣此道行而天
下有不平也哉抑是道也豈自外至而强爲之
耶亦曰物格知至而明無不照故能通天下爲
一身意誠心正而公無不溥故能以一人利天
下盖操之至約而施之則至博也夫子所謂終

耶亦曰物格知至而明無不照故能通天下爲
一身意誠心正而公無不溥故能以一人利天
下蓋操之至約而施之則至博也夫子所謂絜
punctuated: 乎？爲民父母者必不若此也。絜矩君子知民之所好在是也，則欲與之聚，利與之開，眞若有益於我者，而求必得之焉；知民之所惡在是也，則事爲之制，曲爲之防，眞若有損于我者，而求必去之焉。導之於生殖之間而施無不宜，公之於舉錯之際而處無不當。若是者，不謂之民之父母而何哉？誠以父母於子，愛心眞切，志固未始有弗同；天性至親，情亦未始有弗合。君子有以通天下之志而好其所好，則民之遂其好者，亦不忍以其所弗好者及之矣。是雖分相遠也，而相親何以異於一體者乎？有以順天下之情而惡其所惡，則民之違其惡者，亦不忍以其所可惡者及之矣。是雖分相懸也，而相愛有不同於相生者乎？所謂民之父母，信然矣。此道行，而天下有不平也哉？抑是道也，豈自外至而强爲之耶？亦曰物格知至而明無不照，故能通天下爲一身；意誠心正而公無不溥，故能以一人利天下。盖操之至約而施之則至博也。夫子所謂終
translation_en:
…? Those who act as the people's parents surely cannot behave in this way. The gentleman who applies the measuring square of reciprocity knows what the people desire: he gathers for them what they want and opens up sources of benefit for them, seeking surely to obtain these as though they benefited himself. He knows what the people abhor: he makes provision for them in every matter and guards them in every particular, seeking surely to remove these things as though they harmed himself. He guides them in sustaining life and increasing their resources, and everything he provides is fitting; he acts impartially in advancing and dismissing men, and every disposition is appropriate. If such a man is not called the people's parent, what else should he be called?

Indeed, parents love their children truly and deeply, and their aspirations have never been at odds; theirs is the closest natural bond, and their feelings have never failed to accord. When the gentleman can comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven and desire what they desire, the people whose desires are thereby fulfilled likewise cannot bear to inflict upon him what he dislikes. Though their stations are far apart, how does their mutual affection differ from that of a single body? When he can accord with the feelings of all under Heaven and abhor what they abhor, the people who thereby escape what they abhor likewise cannot bear to inflict upon him anything he would find abhorrent. Though their stations are widely separated, is their mutual love any different from that between parents and the children they have brought into being? He truly is what is called the people's parent. If this Way is practiced, could anything under Heaven remain unfair?

Yet does this Way come from outside oneself, to be put into practice by force? It is simply that, when things are investigated and knowledge reaches its fullest extent, one's understanding leaves nothing unilluminated; thus one can unite all under Heaven as a single body. When one's intentions are sincere and one's mind is rectified, one's impartiality extends everywhere; thus one person can benefit all under Heaven. What one holds to is supremely simple, yet its application is supremely broad. This is what the Master meant by saying, “to the end …”

…can be practiced throughout one’s life. What Master Cheng called “extending it fully, so that Heaven and Earth transform and the grasses and trees flourish [?]” is simply this Way. Those charged with being father and mother to this people should understand where to direct their efforts.

Xu Han

The sage commends the great worthy for abiding long in benevolence and thereby encourages the other worthy disciples. How difficult it is to perfect benevolence! By commending the great worthy’s ability to abide in it, the sage can encourage those other worthies who have not yet attained this. I imagine the sage’s meaning thus: benevolence is the complete virtue of the human heart; the heart and benevolence have never been inherently at odds. When the heart nevertheless departs from benevolence, it is because desires encumber it. My Hui alone centers his heart upon benevolence. Supremely discerning, he can detect its incipient stirrings; supremely resolute, he can carry his decisions through. Thus his work of overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety reaches fulfillment, and heavenly principle operates constantly within him. The efficacy of his return to benevolence is apparent for more than a single day; through broad learning and restraint …

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之才竭而德性爲之常用依仁之美盖已不違
于三月吾知其寂然不動心之體也而其仁之
體固渾然而相涵其守矣而需於化矣乎感而
遂通心之用也而其仁之用亦犁然而具足其
復矣而需於純矣乎盖其能久固已幾於安仁
矣過此以往將與天道之不息者而同運焉自
回之餘非不知爲仁也然擇焉而未極其精執
焉而未要於固是以或日至焉而日新之幾未
必緝熈於不已或月至焉而月盛之益大抵作
===
輟於方來吾知其天理亦嘗發見矣而所以存
養之者無成功盖禮雖復而未純也能無頻復
之厲乎德性亦嘗流行矣而所以省察之者無
定力盖已雖克而未盡也能無半塗之廢乎是
其所造殆亦知夫利仁矣作之不已庶乎三月
之不違者而可幾焉是則夫子之與顏子也思
見其止也勵群弟子也思見其進也教亦多術
也如是夫抑論仁之爲德也一也其不一者存
乎其人也故群弟子之於仁當其至焉之域何

translation_en:
…his capacities are fully exerted, and his moral nature is constantly brought into operation. In the excellence of his abiding in benevolence, he has indeed gone three months without departing from it. I know that being still and unmoving is the fundamental substance of his mind; the substance of his benevolence is likewise an undivided whole, each embracing the other. Has he attained steadfast preservation, while still awaiting transformation? Responding to stimulation and thereupon penetrating all things is the functioning of his mind; the functioning of his benevolence is likewise clearly manifest and fully complete. Has he attained a return to goodness, while still awaiting purity? His ability to persevere has indeed already brought him close to resting at ease in benevolence. Advancing beyond this, he will move in concert with the ceaseless operation of the Way of Heaven.

Those other than Hui are not ignorant of how to practice benevolence. Yet their discernment has not reached the utmost refinement, and their grasp has not attained firmness. Thus, some attain it for a day, but the incipient impulse toward daily renewal does not necessarily continue shining without interruption; some attain it for a month, but their gains in monthly growth generally proceed by fits and starts thereafter. I know that heavenly principle has indeed manifested itself in them, yet their efforts to preserve and nurture it have achieved no lasting success. Though they have returned to ritual propriety, they have not yet become pure: can they avoid the peril of repeatedly having to return? Their moral nature has indeed also operated freely, yet their efforts at reflection and scrutiny lack steadfast power. Though they have overcome the self, they have not done so completely: can they avoid abandoning the course halfway? What they have attained probably amounts to understanding the benefit of benevolence. If they exert themselves without ceasing, they may hope to approach the achievement of not departing from it for three months.

Thus, in approving Yan Hui, the Master wished to see him reach his proper resting place; in encouraging the other disciples, he wished to see them advance. Such indeed are the many methods of teaching! Moreover, considered as a virtue, benevolence is one; its variations lie in the people who embody it. Thus, regarding the other disciples’ practice of benevolence, at the point when they attain it, how …

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
塞天地而配道義者也其養之節度當何如哉
彼氣由義生而義則無所為而為者也必也精
義於念慮之微而無欲其所不欲充義於應酬
之著而無為其所不為盖亹亹焉惟知夫義之
當事而果確其功焉義固生氣而生則不可以
力為者也必也安以俟之無見小以覬其大寛
以居之無欲速以必其剛盖休休焉罔知夫效
之攸獲而靜定其心焉夫如是氣宜充矣茍猶
未焉可但已乎彼勿正易流於忘也必也由不
===
欲達諸所欲而精義之功為益密由不為達諸
所為而充義之力為益周庶幾畜極而通而果
確者由之亨斯可焉然勿忘易繼以助也故或
天幾未暢也而用罔以動曰吾以廓吾大也本
體未復也而用壯以逞曰吾以伸吾剛也則是
義襲以取而靜定者為之累矣豈可哉吁有事
勿正而養之直勿忘勿助而養之深此之謂順
也何天地之不可塞何道義之不可配哉抑孟
子前以持志無暴其氣並言矣此獨曰養氣何

punctuated: 塞天地而配道義者也，其養之節度當何如哉？彼氣由義生，而義則無所為而為者也。必也精義於念慮之微，而無欲其所不欲；充義於應酬之著，而無為其所不為。盖亹亹焉，惟知夫義之當事，而果確其功焉。義固生氣，而生則不可以力為者也。必也安以俟之，無見小以覬其大；寛以居之，無欲速以必其剛。盖休休焉，罔知夫效之攸獲，而靜定其心焉。夫如是，氣宜充矣。茍猶未焉，可但已乎？彼勿正易流於忘也，必也由不欲達諸所欲，而精義之功為益密；由不為達諸所為，而充義之力為益周。庶幾畜極而通，而果確者由之亨，斯可焉。然勿忘易繼以助也，故或天幾未暢也，而用罔以動，曰：「吾以廓吾大也。」本體未復也，而用壯以逞，曰：「吾以伸吾剛也。」則是義襲以取，而靜定者為之累矣，豈可哉？吁！有事勿正，而養之直；勿忘勿助，而養之深。此之謂順也。何天地之不可塞？何道義之不可配哉？抑孟子前以持志、無暴其氣並言矣，此獨曰養氣，何
translation_en:
…fills Heaven and Earth and accords with the Way and righteousness. What, then, should govern its cultivation? This qi arises from righteousness, while righteousness means acting without an ulterior purpose. One must discern righteousness precisely in the subtlest stirrings of thought, desiring nothing that one ought not desire; one must extend righteousness fully into the manifest sphere of dealings with others, doing nothing that one ought not do. Working diligently, one attends only to what righteousness requires in each affair and pursues this work with resolve and certainty. Righteousness indeed generates qi, but its growth cannot be forced. One must await it calmly, without glimpsing a small gain and coveting greatness; one must abide in it with ease, without seeking quick results and insisting upon strength. Remaining at ease, one gives no thought to the results to be gained and keeps the mind still and settled. In this way, qi should become full. If it has not yet done so, may one simply stop? Not anticipating results can easily lapse into forgetfulness. One must therefore extend the principle of not desiring what is wrong to all that one desires, making the work of discerning righteousness ever more exact; one must extend the principle of not doing what is wrong to all that one does, making the effort to give righteousness full expression ever more comprehensive. Then, perhaps, accumulation will reach its fullness and flow freely, and the work pursued with resolve and certainty will thereby come to fruition. Only then will it suffice.

Yet not forgetting can easily be followed by attempts to force growth. Thus, when the incipient workings of Heaven have not yet unfolded, someone may act recklessly [?], saying, “By this I enlarge my greatness.” When the original substance has not yet been restored, someone may exert force to assert himself, saying, “By this I extend my strength.” This is to seize qi through isolated acts of righteousness, burdening the mind’s stillness and stability. How could this be acceptable? Ah! Attend to the work without anticipating results, and cultivate qi in uprightness; neither forget it nor force its growth, and cultivate it deeply. This is what is meant by following its natural course. Why should it not fill Heaven and Earth? Why should it not accord with the Way and righteousness? Yet Mengzi earlier spoke of maintaining one’s resolve together with not doing violence to one’s qi. Here he speaks only of cultivating qi. Why…

…why is this so? Maintaining one's resolve is the foundation of nourishing one's vital energy. Neither anticipating results, nor forgetting the task, nor forcing its growth means abiding in reverence to maintain one's resolve: this is the way of uniting the inner and the outer. title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
沃以補其不足偏陂好惡不作于心而念念合
天理之公中以行願賴臣隣以匡其不逮偏黨
反側不施於政而事事即人心之安夫然則慮
罔不臧觀我生而无咎天德以純而敬勝之吉
可必矣動罔或愆履帝位而不疚王道以行而
小疵之悔自无矣其得正之應有如此且交修
之極德容表裏之俱盛出乎身加乎民何者非
和順之英華盖復而至於无妄矣緝熈之餘誠
明内外之並進發乎邇見乎遠何者非篤實之
===
光輝盖孚而至於盈缶矣夫然則明德之昭格
大命自爾其維新典章文物煥然一代之盛也
耿光之覆被民風自爾其丕變禮樂教化蔚然
一時之治也其文明之應又如此是則始而曰
吉者美其德之全也終而曰吉者美其功之成
也然非六五之善變則悔且不免况能吉而又
吉乎抑氣禀之蔽小學問之功大君德以剛為
主五以柔順之資當未濟之時鮮不及矣惟其
識之早而反之力是以人定勝天而吉從之焉

光輝蓋孚而至於盈缶矣夫然則明德之昭格
大命自爾其維新典章文物煥然一代之盛也
耿光之覆被民風自爾其丕變禮樂教化蔚然
一時之治也其文明之應又如此是則始而曰
吉者美其德之全也終而曰吉者美其功之成
也然非六五之善變則悔且不免況能吉而又
吉乎抑氣禀之蔽小學問之功大君德以剛為
主五以柔順之資當未濟之時鮮不及矣惟其
識之早而反之力是以人定勝天而吉從之焉
punctuated: 沃以補其不足，偏陂好惡不作于心，而念念合天理之公；中以行願，賴臣隣以匡其不逮，偏黨反側不施於政，而事事即人心之安。夫然則慮罔不臧，觀我生而无咎，天德以純，而敬勝之吉可必矣；動罔或愆，履帝位而不疚，王道以行，而小疵之悔自无矣。其得正之應有如此。且交修之極，德容表裏之俱盛，出乎身，加乎民，何者非和順之英華？盖復而至於无妄矣。緝熈之餘，誠明内外之並進，發乎邇，見乎遠，何者非篤實之光輝？盖孚而至於盈缶矣。夫然則明德之昭格，大命自爾其維新，典章文物煥然一代之盛也；耿光之覆被，民風自爾其丕變，禮樂教化蔚然一時之治也。其文明之應又如此。是則始而曰吉者，美其德之全也；終而曰吉者，美其功之成也。然非六五之善變，則悔且不免，况能吉而又吉乎？抑氣禀之蔽小，學問之功大，君德以剛為主，五以柔順之資，當未濟之時，鮮不及矣。惟其識之早而反之力，是以人定勝天，而吉從之焉。
translation_en:
…nourishing instruction to remedy his deficiencies, so that biased likes and dislikes do not arise in his heart and every thought accords with the impartiality of Heaven’s principle. Holding to the center to carry out his aspirations, he relies on his ministers and those close to him to correct his shortcomings, so that partiality and perversity find no expression in government and every undertaking accords with what puts the people’s hearts at ease. Thus none of his deliberations is unsound: he “contemplates his own life” and is without blame. His heavenly virtue thereby becomes pure, and the good fortune of reverence prevailing can be assured. None of his actions goes astray: he “occupies the imperial position without unease.” The kingly Way is thereby put into practice, and regret over minor faults naturally disappears. Such are the effects of his attaining correctness.

Moreover, when mutual cultivation reaches its utmost, virtue and outward bearing flourish together, within and without. What issues from his person and extends to the people is all the flowering of harmony and compliance. He has indeed returned to the good and thereby attained freedom from falsity. Through sustained cultivation of brightness, sincerity and understanding advance together, inwardly and outwardly. What emerges nearby and becomes manifest afar is all the radiance of substantial integrity. His sincerity has indeed come to “fill the earthen vessel.” Thus, as his luminous virtue shines forth and reaches above, the great Mandate naturally becomes renewed; institutions, regulations, and cultural achievements splendidly display the flourishing of a dynasty. As his brilliant light spreads its sheltering influence, the people’s customs naturally undergo a great transformation; rites, music, instruction, and moral influence richly display the good government of an age. Such, in turn, are the effects of his cultivated brilliance.

Thus the initial pronouncement of “good fortune” praises the completeness of his virtue, while the concluding pronouncement of “good fortune” praises the completion of his achievement. Yet, without the capacity for beneficial change belonging to the six in the fifth place, regret could scarcely be avoided. How, then, could there be good fortune followed by still more good fortune? Indeed, the obscuration arising from one’s endowment of vital force is slight, while the efficacy of learning is great. Firmness is the principal element of a ruler’s virtue. For the fifth line, endowed with yielding compliance and situated in the time of Before Completion, it would be rare to escape falling short [?]. Only because he recognizes this early and exerts himself vigorously to reverse it does resolute human effort overcome what is given by Heaven, and good fortune follows.

The Great Commentary says that the sages examined Heaven and humanity in creating the Book of Changes, and brought sincerity and reverence to their utmost in using it. Thus, in the transformations of yin and yang, the Way of Heaven is indeed mysterious; then their spirit moves with Heaven …

text:
而命之於穆者有以悉其幾焉事物云為民故
亦云賾矣則患與民同而動之貞勝者有以盡
其詳焉惟明也故知神物之生於天也所當興
惟察也故知民用之冒於幾也所當前於是興
蓍以筮而用之四十有九使夫將有為者揲蓍
以求卦而遠近幽深遂知乎來物矣興龜以卜
而鑽之七十有二使夫將有行者灼龜以審兆
而失得憂虞皆可以前知矣夫卜筮既立聖人
之功業見矣然欲用之以教民又豈不自知所

焉肅然警惕之无怠務使內外昭融而虛靈不
測觀變之下合諸蓍龜而无間不然則深有未
極而欲以通志也聖人亦罔敢以自信矣表裏
澄徹而妙應无方考占之際質諸鬼神而無疑

此則夫以卜筮尚其占者又當何如耶抑蓍龜

澄徹而妙應无方考占之際質諸鬼神而無疑
不然則幾有未研而欲以成務也聖人亦有所
不能矣夫易作於聖人而其用尤不敢以易如
此則夫以卜筮尚其占者又當何如耶抑蓍龜
punctuated: 而命之於穆者，有以悉其幾焉。事物云為，民故亦云賾矣，則患與民同，而動之貞勝者，有以盡其詳焉。惟明也，故知神物之生於天也所當興；惟察也，故知民用之冒於幾也所當前。於是興蓍以筮，而用之四十有九，使夫將有為者揲蓍以求卦，而遠近幽深，遂知乎來物矣。興龜以卜，而鑽之七十有二，使夫將有行者灼龜以審兆，而失得憂虞，皆可以前知矣。夫卜筮既立，聖人之功業見矣。然欲用之以教民，又豈不自知所敬信哉？故无射未嘗不保也，而於此尤齊焉，湛然純一之无二；不覩未嘗不慎也，而於此尤戒焉，肅然警惕之无怠。務使內外昭融，而虛靈不測，觀變之下，合諸蓍龜而无間。不然，則深有未極，而欲以通志也，聖人亦罔敢以自信矣。表裏澄徹，而妙應无方，考占之際，質諸鬼神而無疑。不然，則幾有未研，而欲以成務也，聖人亦有所不能矣。夫易作於聖人，而其用尤不敢以易如此，則夫以卜筮尚其占者，又當何如耶？抑蓍龜
translation_en:
…and, in the profound mystery of Heaven’s mandate, they could fully discern its incipient workings. Affairs, things, speech, and action—the circumstances of the people—are indeed intricate. Yet the sages shared the people’s anxieties, and through constancy prevailing in their actions could comprehend every detail. Through their clarity, they knew that the numinous things produced by Heaven should be brought into use; through their discernment, they knew that the people’s practical needs, encompassing incipient developments, should be anticipated. Thus they instituted divination with milfoil, using forty-nine stalks, so that those about to undertake something could sort the stalks to obtain a hexagram and thereby know what was to come, whether near or distant, hidden or profound. They instituted divination with tortoise shells, boring seventy-two holes in them, so that those about to act could scorch the shells and scrutinize the signs, foreknowing loss and gain, anxieties and dangers. Once these forms of divination had been established, the sages’ achievements became manifest. Yet, wishing to use them to instruct the people, how could they themselves fail to know what to revere and trust?

Thus they never failed to maintain an unwearying devotion, but in this matter they especially purified themselves, remaining serenely single-minded, without divided purpose. They never failed to exercise care over what was unseen, but in this matter they were especially vigilant, solemnly watchful and never remiss. They strove to make their inner and outer selves luminous and harmonious, their minds empty and numinously perceptive beyond measure, so that when observing changes they accorded perfectly with the milfoil and tortoise shells. Otherwise, if there remained depths they had not fully fathomed, even the sages would not dare trust themselves to comprehend the intentions involved. They made themselves clear and transparent within and without, responding wondrously without fixed limits, so that when examining prognostications they could consult the spirits without doubt. Otherwise, if there remained incipient workings they had not thoroughly investigated, even the sages would be unable to bring affairs to completion.

The Changes was created by the sages, yet even they were so unwilling to treat its use lightly. How, then, should those who esteem its prognostications through milfoil and tortoise-shell divination conduct themselves? Now, as for the milfoil and tortoise shells…

Only with someone who understands this can one discuss the sages’ purification and abstinence. After the Qin book burning, the Changes alone survived because of its use in divination, yet the world consequently came to belittle it. Alas! title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
以一身而建天下之中何則中散於事有萬殊
也非制以義焉則物得以眩或失則過或失則
不及矣必也精吾心之權衡研諸慮焉而是非
確乎其攸當絜吾心之矩度効諸動焉而可否
截乎其有方處經事歟則觀會通以行其典禮
惟幾惟康以成務也即諸人心而皆安處變事
歟則妙擬議以成其化裁或損或益以從道也
揆諸天理而皆順夫然則義形而外無不方中
之用於是乎行矣心具乎中本一致也非制以
===
禮焉則欲得以蔽或失則偏或失則倚矣必也
齊戒以神明其德約吾禮焉而微者以之著恂
慄以省察其獨復吾禮焉而危者以之安起知
于意也則誠之於思而非僻不得以或干凛乎
天命之自度也應感于情也則止之以正而淫
佚不得以少肆儼乎天則之惟閑也夫然則禮
立而內無不直中之體於是乎存矣是則德修
而中道斯建中建而君道斯全垂諸後昆且有
餘裕矣况於當時哉抑中一也自其制事之謂

佚不得以少肆儼乎天則之惟閑也夫然則禮
立而內無不直中之〔體〕於是乎存矣是則德修
而中道斯建中建而君道斯全垂諸後昆且有
餘裕矣況於當時哉抑中一也自其制事之謂
punctuated: 以一身而建天下之中。何則？中散於事，有萬殊也。非制以義焉，則物得以眩，或失則過，或失則不及矣。必也精吾心之權衡，研諸慮焉，而是非確乎其攸當；絜吾心之矩度，効諸動焉，而可否截乎其有方。處經事歟，則觀會通以行其典禮，惟幾惟康以成務也，即諸人心而皆安；處變事歟，則妙擬議以成其化裁，或損或益以從道也，揆諸天理而皆順。夫然則義形而外無不方，中之用於是乎行矣。心具乎中，本一致也。非制以禮焉，則欲得以蔽，或失則偏，或失則倚矣。必也齊戒以神明其德，約吾禮焉，而微者以之著；恂慄以省察其獨，復吾禮焉，而危者以之安。起知于意也，則誠之於思，而非僻不得以或干，凛乎天命之自度也；應感于情也，則止之以正，而淫佚不得以少肆，儼乎天則之惟閑也。夫然則禮立而內無不直，中之體於是乎存矣。是則德修而中道斯建，中建而君道斯全，垂諸後昆且有餘裕矣，况於當時哉！抑中一也，自其制事之謂
translation_en:
…through his own person establish the mean for all under Heaven. Why is this? As the mean is distributed among affairs, its manifestations are myriad. Unless affairs are regulated by righteousness, external things can bewilder us: our errors may lie in excess or in deficiency. We must refine the scales and balance of our minds, examining matters in reflection so that judgments of right and wrong are firmly appropriate; we must calibrate the square and measure of our minds, testing them in action so that what is acceptable and unacceptable has clearly defined bounds. In handling ordinary affairs, we must observe how things converge and interconnect in order to carry out the established rites, attending to incipient changes and to well-being in accomplishing our tasks, so that all accords with and satisfies human hearts. In handling exceptional affairs, we must exercise subtle deliberation to achieve fitting adaptations, diminishing or augmenting as necessary to follow the Way, so that everything accords with the principles of Heaven when measured against them. Thus righteousness takes form, and nothing in our outward conduct fails to be square; the functioning of the mean is thereby realized.

The mind possesses the mean, whose basis is a single unity. Unless the mind is regulated by ritual propriety, desires can obscure it: its errors may take the form of partiality or of leaning to one side. We must purify ourselves and observe restraint to make our virtue spiritually luminous, binding ourselves by ritual propriety so that what is subtle becomes manifest; we must examine our solitary selves with trembling vigilance, returning to ritual propriety so that what is precarious becomes secure. When awareness arises in our intentions, we must make it sincere in thought, allowing nothing wrong or perverse to intrude, and reverently measure ourselves by Heaven’s mandate. When our feelings respond to external influences, we must restrain them by what is correct, allowing excess and indulgence no scope whatsoever, and solemnly guard Heaven’s standards. Thus ritual propriety is established, and nothing within fails to be upright; the substance of the mean is thereby preserved.

With virtue thus cultivated, the Way of the mean is established; with the mean established, the Way of the ruler is made complete. There will be more than enough to pass down to later descendants—how much more, then, for the present age! Yet the mean is one: considered in its regulation of affairs, it is called…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
義自其制心之謂禮盖人受天地之中以生而
禮義者中之所出也所以貫體用合內外而一
之道也虞廷精一執中之傳要不出此仲虺之
所得者亦邃矣孟子叙道統及湯謂伊尹萊朱
爲見而知之者而說者以萊朱爲仲虺其信然
哉
亦越文王武王克知三有宅心灼見三有
俊心以敬事上帝立民長伯
許瀚
===
同考試官教諭張批文武迪哲根於正
心之學故宅俊以心相孚爲克知爲灼見古君
臣相與夫豈偶然知此者僅見此作宜錄以爲
官人之則
同考試官教諭周批周家致治之道惟
在得宅俊之賢而其知宅俊之賢又在於君身
以爲之本此作能悉此深得周公告成王知恤
之意

義，自其制心之謂禮。盖人受天地之中以生，而禮義者，中之所出也，所以貫體用、合內外而一之道也。虞廷精一執中之傳，要不出此。仲虺之所得者亦邃矣。孟子叙道統及湯，謂伊尹、萊朱爲見而知之者，而說者以萊朱爲仲虺，其信然哉！
亦越文王、武王，克知三有宅心，灼見三有俊心，以敬事上帝，立民長伯。
許瀚
同考試官教諭張批：文武迪哲，根於正心之學，故宅俊以心相孚，爲克知，爲灼見。古君臣相與，夫豈偶然？知此者僅見此作，宜錄以爲官人之則。
同考試官教諭周批：周家致治之道，惟在得宅俊之賢，而其知宅俊之賢，又在於君身以爲之本。此作能悉此，深得周公告成王知恤之意。
考試官洗馬歐陽批：古雅。
translation_en:
…righteousness; in its regulation of the heart, it is called ritual propriety. Human beings receive the equilibrium of Heaven and Earth at birth, and ritual propriety and righteousness issue from this equilibrium. They are the way by which substance and function are linked, the inner and outer joined, and both made one. The teaching transmitted at Shun’s court—refining discernment, maintaining singleness, and holding fast to the mean—essentially goes no further than this. What Zhong Hui grasped was indeed profound. When Mencius traced the succession of the Way down to Tang, he called Yi Yin and Lai Zhu men who knew it through seeing it. Commentators identify Lai Zhu as Zhong Hui. How true that must be!
“Then there were Kings Wen and Wu, who could know the hearts of the three kinds of officeholders and clearly discern the hearts of the three kinds of outstanding men, thereby reverently serving the Lord on High and establishing leaders and chiefs for the people.”
Xu Han
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The wisdom exercised by Wen and Wu was rooted in the learning of rectifying the heart. Thus, between them and their officeholders and outstanding men, hearts accorded in mutual trust: hence ‘could know’ and ‘clearly discern.’ Could the relationship between ancient rulers and ministers have been merely accidental? This is the only composition I have seen that understands this. It should be recorded as a standard for appointing officials.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The Zhou house’s way of achieving good government lay solely in securing worthy officeholders and outstanding men. Yet its recognition of their worth rested, in turn, upon the ruler’s own person as its foundation. This composition fully understands this point and profoundly grasps the Duke of Zhou’s intention in admonishing King Cheng to understand his responsibilities and take them to heart.”
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Librarian: “Classically elegant.”

考試官左諭德江批簡約
大臣舉前聖迪哲於官人以見其知恤也夫官
人匪哲弗能也自非前聖之知恤安能迪之而
無遺哉宜周公舉以爲成王告也意謂用人知
恤在禹湯固有然者矣亦越我周不有文武之
家法矣乎觀其當純佑之隆秉明哲之迪於三
宅也則有以克知之蓋考跡以觀其衷稽實以
驗其蘊於凡牧民任事守法之有成者莫不洞
然畢察其幾微不徒貌之稽焉而已矣於三俊
===
也則有以灼見之蓋叩擊於敷言之時劑量於
待用之日於凡牧民任事守法之攸宜者莫不
炳然預燭其底裏不徒面之謀焉而已矣是其
德意相孚而宅者得以效其職俊者得以著其
才矣又將何以官之哉彼我文武眷命嘗受之
帝矣而敬事之責寔於宅俊乎是資天民牧焉
天工理焉天法齊焉自爾成能於率作之下矣
仰焉尚何所愧乎寵綏嘗繫之民矣而長伯之
寄亦於宅俊乎是托牧之安焉理之乂焉齊之

大臣舉前聖迪哲於官人，以見其知恤也。夫官人匪哲弗能也，自非前聖之知恤，安能迪之而無遺哉？宜周公舉以爲成王告也。意謂用人知恤，在禹湯固有然者矣。亦越我周，不有文武之家法矣乎？觀其當純佑之隆，秉明哲之迪，於三宅也，則有以克知之。蓋考跡以觀其衷，稽實以驗其蘊，於凡牧民、任事、守法之有成者，莫不洞然畢察其幾微，不徒貌之稽焉而已矣。於三俊也，則有以灼見之。蓋叩擊於敷言之時，劑量於待用之日，於凡牧民、任事、守法之攸宜者，莫不炳然預燭其底裏，不徒面之謀焉而已矣。是其德意相孚，而宅者得以效其職，俊者得以著其才矣。又將何以官之哉？彼我文武，眷命嘗受之帝矣，而敬事之責，寔於宅俊乎是資。天民牧焉，天工理焉，天法齊焉，自爾成能於率作之下矣。仰焉，尚何所愧乎？寵綏嘗繫之民矣，而長伯之寄，亦於宅俊乎是托。牧之安焉，理之乂焉，齊之
translation_en:
Examiner Jiang, Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent, comments: “Concise.”

The great minister cited the former sages’ exercise of wisdom in appointing officials, thereby showing their understanding of the care this required. For without wisdom, one cannot appoint officials. Had the former sages not understood the need for such care, how could they have exercised wisdom without overlooking anything? Fittingly, the Duke of Zhou cited their example in admonishing King Cheng. His meaning was that Yu and Tang had certainly understood the care required in employing men. Coming down to our Zhou, did we not also possess the ancestral example of Kings Wen and Wu?

Observe how, at the height of their wholehearted support for worthy men, they exercised discernment and wisdom. Regarding those occupying the three classes of office, they could truly know them. They examined their deeds to discern their inner intentions and investigated their actual accomplishments to verify their underlying qualities. Among all who had achieved success in shepherding the people, conducting affairs, and upholding laws, there were none whose subtlest qualities they did not thoroughly perceive. They did not merely judge them by their outward appearance. Regarding the worthy candidates for those three classes of office, they could see them clearly. They probed them when they set forth their views and weighed their capacities while they awaited employment. Among all suited to shepherding the people, conducting affairs, and upholding laws, there were none whose innermost qualities they did not clearly discern in advance. They did not merely assess them by their faces. Thus, through mutual trust in virtue and intention, officeholders could discharge their duties and worthy candidates could manifest their talents.

How, then, would they employ these men in office? Our Kings Wen and Wu had received the favoring mandate of the Lord on High, and for the responsibility of reverently serving him they indeed relied upon these officeholders and worthy men. Heaven’s people were shepherded, Heaven’s work was ordered, and Heaven’s laws were applied to bring order. Thus, under their leadership and direction, these men fulfilled their capacities. Looking upward, what cause for shame could the kings still have? Their gracious care and pacification had concerned the people, and they likewise entrusted the charge of leadership to these officeholders and worthy men. Through shepherding them, they brought peace; through administering them, they brought good government; through bringing them into order …

乎是則位天人之兩間一知恤之承藉文武之
家法誠美矣爲後王者惡可不知所法哉雖然
文武之所以知恤者其本尤在於正心蓋其緝
熈敬止敬義夾持則本源澄澈而知人官人之

然哉若後世則以察爲明而以欲相比卒致用

《詩》

「神之弔矣，詒爾多福。民之質矣，日用飲食。羣黎百姓，徧爲爾德。」

徐燦

translation_en:
…in harmony; thus, under comprehensive direction, achievements will naturally follow. Looking down, what further cause would there be for shame? Standing between Heaven and humankind, they know to exercise solicitude throughout, carrying forward the inherited practices of Kings Wen and Wu. How admirable! How could later kings fail to know what they should emulate? Nevertheless, the solicitude of Wen and Wu was rooted above all in rectifying their minds. Through continuous illumination and abiding reverence, sustained jointly by reverence and righteousness, the source became clear and pure; the ultimate standard for discerning people and appointing them to office was already established within themselves. It was surely fitting that their trust should be so deep and their reliance so firm! In later ages, however, rulers took scrutiny for insight and formed attachments according to their desires. In the end, they reversed the proper choices of whom to employ and whom to reject, until Heaven and humankind alike abandoned them. Let those who employ others take warning from this!

The Book of Odes

“The spirits have come to you, bestowing many blessings upon you. The people are settled, daily taking their food and drink. The multitude of common people everywhere practice your virtue.”

Xu Can

Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The words come to an end, but their meaning is inexhaustible. Those who read this will naturally feel refreshed.”

Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: “Its language and thought are concise and antique. It should be included as a model for the many scholars.”

Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor, comments: “It takes the transformation and perfection of all under Heaven as the blessing wished for the ruler, profoundly capturing the meaning of the ode. It therefore merits inclusion.”

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官洗馬歐陽批質而文
考試官左諭德江批敷蔚
臣子托神之福君而歸於天下之化成焉蓋化
成天下王者莫大之福也臣子以是而願其君
焉忠愛之意何如哉意謂吾君以一心之孝敬
嚴四時之祭祀馨香始達而祖考為之居歆臨
之在上若有以見乎其位矣芳臭初升而神明
為之來格質之在傍若有以聞乎其聲矣陟降
之際純嘏於焉而永錫自一身以驗於國家皆
===
簡簡之休也肸蠁之下繁祉於焉而畢集由一
家以達於天下皆穰穰之慶也是果何以見之
哉彼民性不淳君德之累非福也今則智巧不
作咸悃愊以無華日莫不飲也惟知鑿而飲焉
耳舍是何所庸其心大朴無偽舉質實以相尚
日莫不食也惟知耕而食焉耳舍是何所庸其
力然民習未一王化之偏亦非福也今則四海
同風以其導於上者興於下是黎民之敏德即
帝德之廣運也豈非不求助而助之也哉萬民

考試官左諭德江批：敷蔚。
臣子托神之福君，而歸於天下之化成焉。蓋化成天下，王者莫大之福也。臣子以是而願其君焉，忠愛之意何如哉！意謂吾君以一心之孝敬，嚴四時之祭祀。馨香始達，而祖考為之居歆，臨之在上，若有以見乎其位矣；芳臭初升，而神明為之來格，質之在傍，若有以聞乎其聲矣。陟降之際，純嘏於焉而永錫，自一身以驗於國家，皆簡簡之休也；肸蠁之下，繁祉於焉而畢集，由一家以達於天下，皆穰穰之慶也。是果何以見之哉？彼民性不淳，君德之累，非福也。今則智巧不作，咸悃愊以無華。日莫不飲也，惟知鑿而飲焉耳，舍是何所庸其心？大朴無偽，舉質實以相尚。日莫不食也，惟知耕而食焉耳，舍是何所庸其力？然民習未一，王化之偏，亦非福也。今則四海同風，以其導於上者興於下，是黎民之敏德，即帝德之廣運也。豈非不求助而助之也哉？萬民
translation_en:
Examiner Ouyang, Librarian of the Heir Apparent, comments: “Substantial yet refined.”
Examiner Jiang, Left Adviser to the Heir Apparent, comments: “Expansive and luxuriant.”
The minister invokes the spirits to bless his ruler, ultimately locating that blessing in the transformation and perfection of all under Heaven. For a king, no blessing is greater than bringing all under Heaven to perfection through his transforming influence. When a minister wishes this for his ruler, how profound is his loyal affection!
The meaning is that our ruler, with a heart wholly devoted to filial reverence, solemnly performs the sacrifices of the four seasons. As soon as the fragrant offerings reach them, his ancestors take their places and enjoy them. Presiding above, they seem visible in their appointed places. As soon as the sweet fragrance rises, the spirits arrive. Present beside him, they seem almost audible. As they ascend and descend, great blessings are bestowed forever. From his own person to the state, their manifestations are all abundant beneficence. Amid the spirits’ subtle presence, manifold blessings gather in full. From his own family to all under Heaven, these are all bountiful felicities.
How, then, can this actually be seen? If the people’s disposition is not pure, this burdens the ruler’s virtue and is no blessing. Now, however, cunning and artifice do not arise; all are sincere and unadorned. Each day everyone drinks, knowing only to dig wells and drink from them. Beyond this, what need have they to exercise their minds? Utterly simple and without deceit, all esteem plainness and sincerity in one another. Each day everyone eats, knowing only to till the fields and eat their produce. Beyond this, what need have they to exert their strength?
Yet if the people’s customs are not united, the king’s transforming influence is uneven, and this too is no blessing. Now, however, the same customs prevail throughout the Four Seas: what is promoted above flourishes below. Thus the people’s diligent virtue is itself the far-reaching operation of the sovereign’s virtue. Is this not to assist him without being asked for assistance? The myriad people…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
一心以其建諸極者淑諸身是百姓之昭明即
帝德之克明也豈非無所爲而爲之也哉是則
福及一身則其福也有限德及天下則其福也
無窮臣子以是荅君宜矣抑善觀天下者必觀
之民俗民俗之厚薄國家之治忽關焉太古沕
穆不言而化惟數聖人能享其盛世變日趨政
教日繁然後知民之質也其人君之福哉天保
臣子深達乎此後世乃有以豐亨豫大諫其君
而於民之治忽若罔聞知者非惟視民之薄而
===
望君之意亦異乎古人矣噫
無競維人四方其訓之有覺德行四國順
之訏謨定命遠猶辰告敬慎威儀維民
之則
孫滋

一心，以其建諸極者淑諸身，是百姓之昭明，即帝德之克明也，豈非無所爲而爲之也哉？是則福及一身，則其福也有限；德及天下，則其福也無窮。臣子以是荅君，宜矣。抑善觀天下者，必觀之民俗。民俗之厚薄，國家之治忽關焉。太古沕穆，不言而化，惟數聖人能享其盛。世變日趨，政教日繁，然後知民之質也，其人君之福哉！《天保》臣子深達乎此，後世乃有以豐亨豫大諫其君，而於民之治忽若罔聞知者，非惟視民之薄，而望君之意亦異乎古人矣。噫！
「無競維人，四方其訓之。有覺德行，四國順之。訏謨定命，遠猶辰告。敬慎威儀，維民之則。」
孫滋

同考試官教諭梁批：「武公自儆之意，正如此。子能發之，足占所學矣。」
translation_en:
…are of one mind: what the ruler establishes as the supreme standard brings goodness to their persons. Thus the people's luminous understanding is precisely the emperor's virtue of manifesting his brightness. Is this not accomplishing it without deliberate action? Blessings that extend to a single person are limited; when virtue extends throughout the realm, its blessings are inexhaustible. It is fitting that subjects should answer their ruler in these terms. Moreover, anyone skilled at observing the realm must examine the customs of its people. The generosity or meanness of those customs bears upon the state's good government or neglect. In remote antiquity, profound harmony prevailed, and transformation occurred without words; only a few sages could enjoy that flourishing condition. As changes in the world gathered pace and government and instruction grew ever more elaborate, only then did it become clear that the people's simplicity was their ruler's blessing! The subjects who composed “Heaven Protects” (Tianbao) understood this deeply. Yet in later ages there were those who urged their rulers toward abundance, prosperity, ease, and grandeur, while seeming neither to hear nor to know whether the people were well governed or neglected. Not only did they regard the people lightly; their expectations of their rulers also differed from those of the ancients. Alas!
“Unsurpassed strength lies in worthy men;
the four quarters will take instruction from them.
When virtuous conduct is great,
the states in all four quarters follow it.
Great counsels settle commands;
far-reaching plans are announced at the proper time.
Reverent and careful in dignified bearing,
be a model for the people.”
Sun Zi.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: “Expositions of the meaning of the Greater Odes (Daya) that are as lucid, fluent, and dignified as this are exceedingly rare.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: “Duke Wu's intention in admonishing himself was precisely this. Your ability to bring it out is sufficient evidence of your learning.”

賢侯舉道德之應而欲盡其事以求之焉盖道

===
地之性人為貴孰有强於人焉者人惟自視其
小耳能盡其道則無競者在我矣將見以心感
心四方于是乎訓也况其邇者乎亦孰有大於

者在我矣將見以德感德四國於是乎順也况
其小者乎夫道德之應之速也如此而可不知
以自求之乎殆必脩之於政也為謨廣大利天
下而不利一身命令有定勿妄動以疑衆乃為

賢侯舉道德之應而欲盡其事以求之焉。盖道德之感人也尚矣，非賢侯知之以自求，亦焉能盡其事哉？意謂天下有當然之理，則必有自然之應，為其事而無其功者，吾未之見也。是故天地之性，人為貴，孰有强於人焉者？人惟自視其小耳，能盡其道，則無競者在我矣。將見以心感心，四方于是乎訓也，况其邇者乎？亦孰有大於德行焉者？人惟自畏其難耳，能脩其德，則有覺者在我矣。將見以德感德，四國於是乎順也，况其小者乎？夫道德之應之速也如此，而可不知以自求之乎？殆必脩之於政也。為謨廣大，利天下而不利一身；命令有定，勿妄動以疑衆。乃為猷弘遠，計萬世而不計一時；播告以辰，勿慢令
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor, comments: Duke Wu’s admonitions are directed precisely toward examining oneself and cultivating one’s own character. Most writers give equal weight to the two aspects, badly misjudging their relative importance. This essay grasps the meaning intimately and expresses it concisely and aptly. I select it.
Examiner Ouyang, Librarian of the Heir Apparent, comments: Meticulous.
Examiner Jiang, Left Admonisher, comments: Simple and unadorned.
The worthy lord invokes the responses elicited by the Way and virtue, wishing to fulfill every requisite undertaking in order to obtain them. The power of the Way and virtue to move others has indeed long been recognized. Unless the worthy lord understood this and sought its realization within himself, how could he fulfill all these undertakings? The meaning is this: wherever there is a principle prescribing what ought to be, there must be a response that follows naturally. I have never seen anyone carry out the requisite undertaking without achieving its result. Thus, among the beings endowed with life by Heaven and Earth, human beings are most noble. What could be stronger than human beings? People merely regard themselves as insignificant. If I can fulfill the human Way, then unsurpassed strength lies within me. We shall then see heart moving heart, and the four quarters taking instruction accordingly—how much more those nearby! And what could be greater than virtuous conduct? People merely shrink from its difficulty. If I can cultivate my virtue, then manifest greatness lies within me. We shall then see virtue moving virtue, and the states of the four quarters submitting accordingly—how much more the smaller ones! If the response to the Way and virtue is so swift, can one fail to understand that one must seek it within oneself? Surely one must cultivate it in government. Let plans be broad in scope, benefiting all under Heaven rather than oneself alone; let commands be settled, without rash changes that leave the multitude in doubt. Let designs be far-reaching, taking account of ten thousand generations rather than a single moment; issue proclamations at the proper times, and do not delay commands…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
以致期焉其政之所達罔有不臧者矣又必脩
之於身也瞻視尊嚴儼然有威之可畏而暴慢
之斯逺容止端莊肅然有儀之可象而非僻之
不干其身之所履罔有不欽者矣由是大觀在
上行而為天下則矣所謂四方訓之者不在此
乎皇建有極動而為天下道矣所謂四國順之
者不在此乎否則有一未盡即道德之累其何
以為民表哉抑武公年逾於耄矣夫豈好如是
之過勞耶書曰惟聖罔念作狂惟狂克念作聖
===
一息尚存此志不容少懈道固然也然此猶其
脩諸顯者耳若夫不愧屋漏則其功愈密而德
愈深矣睿聖之稱豈偶然哉後世有身未老而
衰功未成而怠者烏足以與此

punctuated:
以致期焉，其政之所達罔有不臧者矣。又必脩之於身也：瞻視尊嚴，儼然有威之可畏，而暴慢之斯逺；容止端莊，肅然有儀之可象，而非僻之不干。其身之所履罔有不欽者矣。由是大觀在上，行而為天下則矣，所謂四方訓之者不在此乎？皇建有極，動而為天下道矣，所謂四國順之者不在此乎？否則有一未盡，即道德之累，其何以為民表哉？抑武公年逾於耄矣，夫豈好如是之過勞耶？《書》曰：「惟聖罔念作狂，惟狂克念作聖。」一息尚存，此志不容少懈，道固然也。然此猶其脩諸顯者耳。若夫不愧屋漏，則其功愈密而德愈深矣。睿聖之稱豈偶然哉？後世有身未老而衰、功未成而怠者，烏足以與此？

春秋

秋，公子遂、叔孫得臣如齊。〔文公十有八年〕
歸父還自晉，至笙，遂奔齊。〔宣公十有八年〕
三月，取鄆。〔昭公元年〕
叔孫舍至自晉。〔昭公二十有四年〕
translation_en:
…thereby causing deadlines to be missed. Wherever his government extends, nothing will fail to be good. He must also cultivate himself: his gaze must be dignified and grave, displaying an awe-inspiring majesty, so that violence and arrogance are kept far away; his bearing must be upright and composed, displaying a solemn deportment worthy of imitation, so that perversity and misconduct do not intrude. Nothing in his personal conduct will lack reverence. Thus, as a great exemplar on high, his conduct becomes a standard for all under Heaven. Is this not what is meant by the four quarters following his instruction? He grandly establishes the supreme standard, and his actions become a guiding way for all under Heaven. Is this not what is meant by the states in all four quarters obeying him? Otherwise, even one point left unfulfilled would blemish his moral cultivation. How could he serve as an exemplar for the people?

Moreover, Duke Wu was already past eighty. Surely he did not delight in such excessive exertion? The Book of Documents says: “If a sage fails to reflect, he becomes a fool; if a fool can reflect, he becomes a sage.” As long as a single breath remains, this resolve must not slacken in the slightest: such, indeed, is the Way. Yet this still concerns only his cultivation in its visible aspects. As for remaining free of shame even in the secluded recesses of his chamber, his effort was still more painstaking and his virtue still more profound. Could his reputation for sagely wisdom have been accidental? How could those in later ages whose vigor declines before they grow old, and who grow indolent before their work is accomplished, possibly compare with him?

Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, Prince Sui and Shusun Dechen went to Qi. 〔Eighteenth year of Duke Wen.〕

Guifu returned from Jin, reached Sheng, and thereupon fled to Qi. 〔Eighteenth year of Duke Xuan.〕

In the third month, Yun was taken. 〔First year of Duke Zhao.〕

Shusun She arrived back from Jin. 〔Twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhao.〕
