之
君相獻
第四問
徐燦
punctuated:
成其可。有所謂否而有可焉，則獻其可以去其否。都俞吁咈，眞若堯舜禹臯交會于一堂；迪畏棐恭，眞若文武周召相際于一時。恤煢獨，釋逋負，薄稅斂，務有以厚之而不困；蠲煩苛，黜貪酷，時工作，務有以生之而不傷；雪寃抑，議功能，省刑罰，務有以通其情而不盡。如是，則政何有不善，民何有不安，而天變何有不弭也哉？若夫百祥日降，四靈畢至，此固體信達順之道，然有之靡益，無之靡補，亦豈有識者之樂道哉？孟子曰：「欲爲君，盡君道；欲爲臣，盡臣道。二者皆法堯舜而已矣。」不以舜之所以事堯事君，不敬其君者也；不以堯之所以治民治民，賊其民者也。愚也敢誦斯言，以爲今日之君相獻。

第四問

徐燦
translation_en:
…to bring what is acceptable to completion. Where something is deemed unacceptable yet contains something acceptable, they should present what is acceptable so as to remove what is unacceptable. Their exchanges of assent and dissent would truly resemble Yao, Shun, Yu, and Gao Yao meeting in one hall; their guidance toward reverent awe and assistance in respectful service would truly resemble Kings Wen and Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao coming together in one age. They should care for the forlorn and solitary, remit outstanding debts, and lighten taxation, striving to enrich the people's livelihood without impoverishing them. They should abolish burdensome and harsh requirements, dismiss corrupt and cruel officials, and undertake public works at appropriate seasons, striving to sustain the people without harming them. They should redress wrongful accusations and oppression, assess merit and ability, and reduce punishments, striving to understand the people's circumstances without exhausting them [?]. If this were done, how could government fail to be good, the people fail to be secure, or Heaven's anomalous manifestations fail to subside?

As for a hundred auspicious signs descending daily and all four numinous creatures appearing, these indeed belong to the way of embodying trustworthiness and attaining harmony. Yet their presence brings no benefit and their absence supplies no remedy [?]; how could discerning people delight in discussing them? Mencius said: “If one wishes to be a ruler, one must fully carry out the ruler's way; if one wishes to be a minister, one must fully carry out the minister's way. Both consist simply in taking Yao and Shun as models.” To fail to serve one's ruler as Shun served Yao is to show disrespect for one's ruler; to fail to govern the people as Yao governed them is to injure one's people. Foolish though I am, I venture to recite these words and offer them to the ruler and chief ministers of our day.

Fourth Policy Question

Xu Can

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
又不幸而夷簡秉政事多報罷□□□
既不能賛成于西歲幣之遺又不免有增
于北志沮氣索咎當誰執哉神宗有見干
此厲精講武準周官以飭邦計此其志卽
藝祖之志也志偶不終而卒蒙釀亂之名
則安石作氣之過不免于助長之敝焉爾
矣於帝乎何尤洪惟我
太祖高皇帝掃胡塵於中國以大一統之基
太宗文皇帝建神都於上游以扼三邊之吭則

translation_en:
…Moreover, unfortunately, when Yijian held power, proposals were often rejected. □□□ could not help bring matters to a successful conclusion in the west [?], while the annual gifts of tribute inevitably increased in the north. With resolve thwarted and spirit exhausted, who should bear the blame? Emperor Shenzong perceived this, applied himself vigorously to military preparedness, and took the Offices of Zhou as his standard for putting the state's finances in order. His ambition was precisely that of the Song founding emperor, Taizu. That his ambition happened to remain unfulfilled, and that he ultimately incurred the reputation of having fomented disorder, resulted merely from Anshi's excessive zeal and the harm of trying to force growth. What blame attaches to the emperor?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao swept the dust of the Hu from the Central Lands, thereby establishing the foundation of a great unification; Emperor Taizong Wen established the sacred capital in a commanding upstream position, thereby gripping the throat of the three frontiers. Thus, what Gaozu of Han, with the might acquired through personally fighting a hundred battles, could not subdue, and what Song Taizu, exhausting a lifetime's planning, could not acquire, our dynasty alone obtained, enjoying the fullness of its glory. Yet their divine plans and sagely deliberations were recorded in the Ancestral Instructions. One injunction says, “Against the Hu and Rong, preparations must be scrupulously maintained”; another says, “Annan is not to be attacked.” How profound was their planning for their sagely sons and divine grandsons through countless generations! Reflecting on the injunction to maintain careful preparations, I have considered that today's three frontiers and six garrisons are, for the most part, all places of the Zhou, Qin, and Han…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
唐之畿輔而燕晋之故都也當時以國爲
守即有虜患譬之蚊䖟驅之耳慨自石晋
失險之後而世之責宋者槩曰聲容盛而
武備衰議論多而成功少不知太阿倒持
且授之柄矣又何施於登龜伐鼉之時乎
由是觀之則六鎮之險尺寸皆金湯也而
可不謹備之哉是故大寧之遷宜復也是
山後之阨塞而遼陽宣大之掎角也不然
則如丘文莊之議移之永薊内拱都城而
===
外護
陵寢亦可也東勝之守宜復也是河套之控
阨而黠虜之甌脫也不然則如李文正之
議阻河爲固東連大同而西接寧夏亦可
也至若哈密之失守亦不刺之竄據則又
甘肅藩籬之隱憂也彼馬端肅之績張兵
侍之策既不復尋矣無已姑亦收復海西
諸番置之哈密近境西制土番北制瓦剌
又不亦可乎三險既復而後於

punctuated: 唐之畿輔，而燕晋之故都也。當時以國爲守，即有虜患，譬之蚊䖟，驅之耳。慨自石晋失險之後，而世之責宋者槩曰：「聲容盛而武備衰，議論多而成功少。」不知太阿倒持，且授之柄矣，又何施於登龜伐鼉之時乎？由是觀之，則六鎮之險，尺寸皆金湯也，而可不謹備之哉？是故大寧之遷宜復也，是山後之阨塞，而遼陽、宣大之掎角也。不然，則如丘文莊之議，移之永薊，内拱都城，而外護陵寢，亦可也。東勝之守宜復也，是河套之控阨，而黠虜之甌脫也。不然，則如李文正之議，阻河爲固，東連大同，而西接寧夏，亦可也。至若哈密之失守，亦不刺之竄據，則又甘肅藩籬之隱憂也。彼馬端肅之績、張兵侍之策，既不復尋矣。無已，姑亦收復海西諸番，置之哈密近境，西制土番，北制瓦剌，又不亦可乎？三險既復，而後於
translation_en:
…and Tang, and the former capitals of Yan and Jin. In those days, the realm itself served as a defensive barrier; even when incursions by the northern peoples occurred, they were like mosquitoes and horseflies, merely to be driven off. Alas, after the Shi house of Jin surrendered the strategic terrain, those who criticized the Song generally said: “Its ceremonial splendor flourished while its military preparations declined; it had much discussion but little accomplishment.” They did not understand that the sword Tai’a had been held backward, its hilt handed to the enemy. What could then be done when the time came to “mount the tortoise and strike the alligator” [?]? Viewed in this light, every inch of the strategic terrain of the Six Garrisons is a rampart of metal and a moat of boiling water. How could we fail to guard it carefully?

Thus, the relocation of Daning should be reversed. It is a strategic stronghold beyond the mountains and provides mutually supporting defense with Liaoyang, Xuanfu, and Datong. Alternatively, following the proposal of Qiu Wenzhuang, it could be moved to Yongping and Jizhou, shielding the capital on the inside and protecting the imperial tombs on the outside. This too would be acceptable. The garrison at Dongsheng should be restored. It commands the strategic approaches to the Hetao region and is an outpost used by the cunning northern enemy. Alternatively, following the proposal of Li Wenzheng, we could rely on the river as a defensive barrier, linking up with Datong to the east and Ningxia to the west. This too would be acceptable.

As for the loss of Hami and its occupation by the fugitive Yibula, these constitute a further latent threat to Gansu’s protective outer defenses. The achievements of Ma Duansu and the plans of Zhang, Vice Minister of War, have no longer been followed up. If there is no other course, might we not provisionally bring the various tribal peoples of Haixi back under our control and settle them near Hami, to check the Tibetans to the west and the Oirats to the north? Once these three strategic positions have been recovered, then, with regard to…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖祖謹備之訓嗣服有光矣或乃曰今日之
力方屈事勢難為而顧為是闊論哉則愚
既曰志定而氣自勝文武之聖天保采薇
之治亦自一念之憂勤成之耳況以
皇上大有為之資為
聖子神孫千萬禩之計又何所撓而不可哉所
願定志於上責成于下制閫任韓范之良
分麾擇趙辛之畧修屯政以備軍儲整鹾
法以佐邊計而
===
朝廷之上於德業則益以修於紀綱則益以
振必使吾之氣勝浩然而塞乎兩間則無
所為而弗利矣不然則宋之敝亦誠已可
監矣又嘗自不征之訓而繹思之安南者
秦漢以來郡縣之故地固也然歷代羈縻
叛服靡常實未有能食其土之毛者至宋
則封王稱國不復為中國之郡縣矣我
聖祖開國之初其王陳氏首先納欵是以特懷
之而有不征之

分麾擇趙辛之畧修屯政以備軍儲整鹺
法以佐邊計而
===
朝廷之上於德業則益以修於紀綱則益以
振必使吾之氣勝浩然而塞乎兩間則無
所爲而弗利矣不然則宋之敝亦誠已可
監矣又嘗自不征之訓而繹思之安南者
秦漢以來郡縣之故地固也然歷代羈縻
叛服靡常實未有能食其土之毛者至宋
則封王稱國不復爲中國之郡縣矣我
聖祖開國之初其王陳氏首先納欵是以特懷
之而有不征之
punctuated:
聖祖謹備之訓，嗣服有光矣。或乃曰：「今日之力方屈，事勢難為，而顧為是闊論哉？」則愚既曰：「志定而氣自勝。」文武之聖，天保、采薇之治，亦自一念之憂勤成之耳。況以皇上大有為之資，為聖子神孫千萬禩之計，又何所撓而不可哉？所願定志於上，責成于下，制閫任韓范之良，分麾擇趙辛之畧，修屯政以備軍儲，整鹾法以佐邊計。而朝廷之上，於德業則益以修，於紀綱則益以振，必使吾之氣勝，浩然而塞乎兩間，則無所為而弗利矣。不然，則宋之敝亦誠已可監矣。
又嘗自不征之訓而繹思之：安南者，秦漢以來郡縣之故地，固也。然歷代羈縻，叛服靡常，實未有能食其土之毛者。至宋，則封王稱國，不復為中國之郡縣矣。我聖祖開國之初，其王陳氏首先納欵，是以特懷之，而有不征之
translation_en:
…then, in carrying on the imperial inheritance, glory would be brought to the Sagely Founder’s injunction to maintain vigilant defenses. Someone may say: “Our strength is now exhausted, and circumstances make action difficult; yet you indulge in such sweeping proposals?” My humble answer has already been: “Once resolve is fixed, vital force will naturally prevail.” Even the sage achievements of Kings Wen and Wu, and the good government celebrated in “Heaven Protects” (Tian bao) and “Gathering Ferns” (Cai wei), were accomplished through a single steadfast commitment to anxious diligence. How much more, then, with Your Majesty’s capacity for great achievement, when planning for your sagely descendants for countless generations! What obstacle could thwart this undertaking or make it impossible? My wish is that resolve be fixed above and responsibility for accomplishment imposed below; that regional military commands be entrusted to men as worthy as Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan, and subordinate commands assigned to men with the strategic talents of Zhao Chongguo and Xin Qingji; that military agricultural administration be improved to provision the armies, and the salt regulations put in order to support frontier finances. At court, let moral achievement be cultivated still further and governing discipline strengthened still further. We must ensure that our vital force prevails, vast and overflowing between Heaven and Earth; then nothing we undertake will fail to prosper. Otherwise, the failings of the Song surely already offer a warning.
I have also reflected upon the injunction against military expeditions. Annan was indeed formerly territory administered as commanderies and counties from Qin and Han times onward. Yet successive dynasties maintained only loose control, and its rebellion and submission were inconstant; in truth, none could enjoy the produce of its land. Under the Song, its ruler was enfeoffed as king and its territory styled a kingdom; it was no longer administered as Chinese commanderies and counties. When our Sagely Founder first established the dynasty, its king, of the Chen family, was foremost in tendering submission. The Founder therefore showed him particular favor and issued the injunction against military expeditions…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
訓焉若我
太宗所以奮討黎季犛者以其簒主殺使不得
已而用兵也時則爲陳氏立後也我
宣廟所以繼討黎利者以其據地殘民亦不得
已而用兵也時則爲我之郡縣也今安所
爲而可勤吾之王師哉將謂推亡固存如
太宗耶則莫登庸者賊也而黎利者固亦逸賊
也利既幸而得國又幸而傳且數世矣天
道好還今乃從而報之則吾亦安從而推
===
之而固之哉將謂保大定功如
宣廟耶則交故瘴鄉也山箐之深阻蝮虺之蠢
生兵有不戰而死者若我永樂之執黎季
犛也未幾而叛者繼起迄宣德而莫定頻
年宿兵魯不得馘利首以奏凱而利且挾
陳暠請封矣是交之亂亦豈可以率爾而
定哉將謂中國故地欲乘其亂而復之耶
則自漢馬伏波之標銅柱交已委之炎荒
矣及我張輔之取之也提師數十萬轉輸

punctuated: 訓焉。若我太宗所以奮討黎季犛者，以其簒主殺使，不得已而用兵也，時則爲陳氏立後也。我宣廟所以繼討黎利者，以其據地殘民，亦不得已而用兵也，時則爲我之郡縣也。今安所爲而可勤吾之王師哉？將謂推亡固存，如太宗耶？則莫登庸者賊也，而黎利者固亦逸賊也。利既幸而得國，又幸而傳且數世矣。天道好還，今乃從而報之，則吾亦安從而推之而固之哉？將謂保大定功，如宣廟耶？則交故瘴鄉也，山箐之深阻，蝮虺之蠢生，兵有不戰而死者。若我永樂之執黎季犛也，未幾而叛者繼起，迄宣德而莫定，頻年宿兵，魯不得馘利首以奏凱，而利且挾陳暠請封矣。是交之亂，亦豈可以率爾而定哉？將謂中國故地，欲乘其亂而復之耶？則自漢馬伏波之標銅柱，交已委之炎荒矣。及我張輔之取之也，提師數十萬，轉輸
translation_en:
…an injunction to that effect. As for our Emperor Taizong’s vigorous campaign against Li Jili, he resorted to arms only because Li had usurped his ruler’s position and killed an envoy, leaving no alternative. The purpose then was to establish a successor to the Chen house. Our Emperor Xuanzong subsequently campaigned against Li Li because he occupied territory and brutalized the people; he too resorted to arms only because there was no alternative. At that time, the territory constituted our prefectures and counties. For what purpose, then, could we now justifiably put our royal army to such exertion?
Would one propose to overthrow the doomed and secure those who should survive, as Taizong did? Mo Dengyong is indeed a rebel, but Li Li was himself a rebel who escaped punishment. Li was fortunate enough to obtain the kingdom, and fortunate again to transmit it through several generations. Heaven’s way brings retribution; now that repayment has followed, on what grounds should we intervene to overthrow one house and secure the other?
Would one propose to preserve our greatness and consolidate our achievements, as Xuanzong did? Jiao has always been a land of pestilential vapors. Its mountain thickets are deep and difficult to traverse, and venomous snakes teem there; soldiers die without even fighting. When we captured Li Jili during the Yongle reign, further rebels arose before long. Even by the Xuande reign the region remained unsettled. Troops were stationed there year after year, yet [?] they could not take Li’s head and announce victory; Li even used Chen Gao as a pretext to request enfeoffment. Could the disorder in Jiao possibly be settled by precipitate action?
Would one say that this was formerly Chinese territory and seek to take advantage of its disorder to recover it? Since Ma, the Han General Who Calms the Waves, erected his bronze pillars, Jiao had already been consigned to the torrid wilderness. When our Zhang Fu took it, he led an army of several hundred thousand and transported supplies…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
三省閱兩載而後平旣而郡且縣之矣撫
之以黄忠宣矣旣十年而計其歲徵曾不
足以償所亡之萬一則區區數年郡縣之
虛名又何有於我哉或則曰
大聖人之撫世附夷之告變義必有處也可遂
但已乎曰語有之帝王之待要荒也有威
讓之令有文告之辭言未遽勤兵於遠也
乃者
聖天子發綸音定
===
廟謨委經畧於撫臣責整備於制帥先聲後
實以德為威持志養氣之善雖古帝王以
全取勝之道不是過矣所願石畫之臣卒
有以賛其成耳不然則漢武窮兵之悔非
聖治之所樂聞矣抑夷狄之為中國患也
其運有盛衰其勢有堅瑕其時有緩急其
幾有利害而吾之御之也要貴有權焉若
今之虜運則寖盛矣勢則堅而時則已急
矣其幾則也先火篩之釁已為之履霜矣

虛名又何有於我哉或則曰
大聖人之撫世附夷之告變義必有處也可遂
但已乎曰語有之帝王之待要荒也有威
讓之令有文告之辭言未遽勤兵於遠也
乃者
聖天子發綸音定
===
廟謨委經畧於撫臣責整備於制帥先聲後
實以德爲威持志養氣之善雖古帝王以
全取勝之道不是過矣所願石畫之臣卒
有以贊其成耳不然則漢武窮兵之悔非
聖治之所樂聞矣抑夷狄之爲中國患也
其運有盛衰其勢有堅瑕其時有緩急其
幾有利害而吾之御之也要貴有權焉若
今之虜運則寖盛矣勢則堅而時則已急
矣其幾則也先火篩之釁已爲之履霜矣
punctuated:
三省，閱兩載而後平。旣而郡且縣之矣，撫之以黄忠宣矣。旣十年而計其歲徵，曾不足以償所亡之萬一，則區區數年郡縣之虛名，又何有於我哉？或則曰：「大聖人之撫世，附夷之告變，義必有處也，可遂但已乎？」曰：「語有之：帝王之待要荒也，有威讓之令，有文告之辭，言未遽勤兵於遠也。乃者，聖天子發綸音，定廟謨，委經畧於撫臣，責整備於制帥，先聲後實，以德為威。持志養氣之善，雖古帝王以全取勝之道，不是過矣。所願石畫之臣，卒有以賛其成耳。不然，則漢武窮兵之悔，非聖治之所樂聞矣。」
抑夷狄之為中國患也，其運有盛衰，其勢有堅瑕，其時有緩急，其幾有利害，而吾之御之也，要貴有權焉。若今之虜，運則寖盛矣，勢則堅而時則已急矣，其幾則也先、火篩之釁，已為之履霜矣。
translation_en:
…three provinces, and only after two years was the region pacified. We then established prefectures and counties there and entrusted its pacification to Huang Zhongxuan. Yet after ten years, when its annual revenues were reckoned, they did not suffice to repay even one ten-thousandth of what had been lost. What, then, did we gain from the empty name of possessing prefectures and counties for those few years?
Someone may say: “When a great sage governs the world and dependent foreign peoples report upheaval, surely righteousness requires some response. Can we simply let the matter rest?” I reply: “There is a saying: in dealing with the distant outer regions, emperors and kings issue commands of stern reproof and proclamations of admonition. This means that they do not hastily send armies to toil far away. Recently, our sagely Son of Heaven issued his imperial pronouncement and settled the court’s strategy, entrusting strategic direction to the grand coordinator and charging the regional commander with preparations. He put a declaration of resolve before action and made virtue the source of his awe-inspiring authority. In steadfastness of purpose and the nurturing of resolve, even the ancient emperors’ and kings’ way of achieving victory while preserving all intact did not surpass this. My only wish is that ministers with sound plans may ultimately help bring it to completion. Otherwise, the regret of Emperor Wu of Han over exhausting his forces in warfare is something we would not gladly hear of under this sagely government.”
Moreover, when foreign peoples threaten the Central Kingdom, their fortunes wax and wane, their strength has firm and vulnerable points, the circumstances permit delay or demand urgency, and the incipient developments offer advantage or danger. In resisting them, what matters above all is judging circumstances flexibly. As for the northern foes today, their fortunes are gradually rising, their position is strong, and the situation has already become urgent. As for warning signs, the troubles caused by Yexian and Huoshai have already been like treading on frost—a forewarning of the hard ice to come.

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
若南夷之患則異于是且自古用兵如宋
如元皆未有得志於南者而北則漢武之
遺烈可想而見也是北雖形難而實則可
圖也況一大創之即有百十年之利乎南
雖形易而實則不可以甞試也萬一衂焉
不有逆顏行之辱乎是在經國者權之旣
審矣藿食之慮何足以與知之

不有逆顔行之辱乎是在經國者權之既
審矣藿食之慮何足以與知之
punctuated: 若南夷之患，則異于是。且自古用兵，如宋、如元，皆未有得志於南者；而北則漢武之遺烈，可想而見也。是北雖形難，而實則可圖也，況一大創之，即有百十年之利乎？南雖形易，而實則不可以甞試也。萬一衂焉，不有逆顏行之辱乎？是在經國者權之旣審矣，藿食之慮，何足以與知之？
translation_en: As for the threat posed by the southern peoples, the situation is different. Since antiquity, those who have waged war in the south, including the Song and Yuan dynasties, have never achieved their aims there. In the north, however, the enduring achievements of Emperor Wu of Han can readily be envisaged. Thus, although the north appears difficult, success there is actually attainable. Moreover, would not a single crushing defeat inflicted upon them bring benefits lasting decades or even a century? Although the south appears easy, in reality it is no place to try our luck. Should we suffer a defeat, would we not incur the humiliation of a reverse at the battlefront? Those who administer the state have already weighed this matter carefully. How could the concerns of one who subsists on bean leaves merit any part in their deliberations?

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the fifth year after Our Emperor ascended the throne, he examined scholars with policy questions in the great court. Your servant Qu received the gracious award of a degree with distinction. Barely ten years later, I was commanded to come together with your servant Rubi to preside over the Yingtian Provincial Examination. Having first advanced through literary composition, I now, in turn, advance scholars to court through their compositions. Among the honors bestowed upon a subject, this is indeed exceptional. Nevertheless, I cannot be without apprehension.

When a dynasty rises, it receives its mandate from Heaven, but where it emerges depends upon the land. When talented men are born, they embody the spiritual potency concentrated in the land, but their flourishing depends upon the ruler. The kingly aura of the southeast first emerged in Feng and Pei, inaugurating the Han dynasty’s four-hundred-year enterprise. Yet even this was insufficient to realize its full flourishing, and it lingered…

title: 嘉靖十六年應天府鄉試錄
text:
蓄汪濊積千百餘年我
太祖高皇帝起義定遠定鼎金陵以
混一天下此固貞元會合然一
時勳臣出於東南者為盛亦既
漸漬百五十年矣我
皇上起自江漢入
正大統而名臣碩輔出於南國者
===
後先相望亦既涵泳十有六年
矣地之靈也
上之化也其弗信矣乎顧臣未之能
報也其將曰藉手豪傑以幾萬
分一而或有不得若人焉臣於
是有餘懼矣臣聞之萬物出乎
震齊乎巽相見乎離皆自東而

punctuated: 蓄汪濊，積千百餘年。我太祖高皇帝起義定遠，定鼎金陵，以混一天下。此固貞元會合，然一時勳臣出於東南者為盛，亦既漸漬百五十年矣。我皇上起自江漢，入正大統，而名臣碩輔出於南國者，後先相望，亦既涵泳十有六年矣。地之靈也，上之化也，其弗信矣乎？顧臣未之能報也。其將曰藉手豪傑，以幾萬分一，而或有不得若人焉，臣於是有餘懼矣。臣聞之：萬物出乎震，齊乎巽，相見乎離，皆自東而
translation_en: …stored up in vast abundance, accumulating for more than a thousand years. Our Emperor Taizu Gao raised his righteous forces at Dingyuan and established his capital at Jinling, thereby unifying all under Heaven. This was indeed the conjunction of cosmic completion and renewal; yet among the meritorious ministers of that age, those from the southeast were especially numerous. For a hundred and fifty years now, this region has been steeped in the dynasty’s nurturing influence. Our present Emperor arose from the Jiang–Han region and entered upon the legitimate imperial succession. Eminent ministers and great counsellors from the southern lands have followed one another in unbroken succession, and for sixteen years now they have been immersed in his nurturing influence. This is the numinous potency of the land and the transforming influence of His Majesty: can these indeed be doubted? Yet your servant has been unable to repay them. I might hope to draw upon outstanding men to repay even one ten-thousandth of this bounty; but should I fail to obtain such men, your servant would have ample cause for fear. Your servant has heard it said: “The myriad things come forth in Zhen, are brought into harmonious order in Xun, and become visible to one another in Li.” All proceed from the east and…
